nodes.label: David Sinclair
nodes.description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). Directionally, the discovery establishes SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity research. This launched the modern sirtuin field, and it connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics. By showing that resveratrol extends yeast lifespan through Sir2, Sinclair bridged the caloric-restriction and sirtuin fields. This work catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development and made SIRT1 a central target in geroscience.

nodes.label: SIRT1 as CR mediator
nodes.description: David Sinclair identified SIRT1 as a mediator of caloric-restriction benefits and, in a landmark 2003 study, discovered resveratrol as a sirtuin-activating compound (STAC). Directionally, the discovery establishes SIRT1/STAC centrality to longevity research. This launched the modern sirtuin field, and it connects basic yeast findings to mammalian therapeutics. By showing that resveratrol extends yeast lifespan through Sir2, Sinclair bridged the caloric-restriction and sirtuin fields. This work catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development and made SIRT1 a central target in geroscience.

nodes.label: Resveratrol as STAC
nodes.description: In 2003, Sinclair showed resveratrol extends yeast lifespan via Sir2 and later demonstrated parallel effects in higher organisms, discovering it as the first STAC. Directionally, the discovery sits upstream of the STAC concept. This catalyzed decades of sirtuin-drug development, and it remains a seminal finding in geroscience. By identifying a natural compound that activates sirtuins, Sinclair provided the prototype for pharmacologically engaging longevity pathways. The STAC concept has since driven the search for more potent and specific sirtuin activators for therapeutic use.

nodes.label: Sirtris Pharmaceuticals
nodes.description: Sinclair co-founded Sirtris Pharmaceuticals (later acquired by GlaxoSmithKline) to develop STACs such as SRT1720 and SRT2104 as therapeutics. Directionally, the academic discovery was translated into a company. This drove clinical translation of sirtuin activators, and it illustrates the bench-to-bedside path of sirtuin research. By commercializing STACs, Sirtris aimed to develop drugs that reproduce the metabolic benefits of caloric restriction. Although clinical outcomes were mixed, the company's formation validated sirtuins as a druggable target class and stimulated industrial interest in longevity biology.

nodes.label: ICE Mouse model
nodes.description: The Sinclair lab developed the ICE Mouse to test the RCM hypothesis using mutation-free double-strand breaks. Directionally, the model enables tests of epigenetic aging. This provided key evidence for the Information Theory of Aging, and it is a methodological contribution alongside the theoretical framework. By engineering a system to induce faithful DNA breaks, Sinclair created a tool to separate epigenetic from genetic contributions to aging. The ICE Mouse's results have made it a centerpiece of the argument that aging results from loss of epigenetic information.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (via Hes1 deacetylation)
nodes.description: SIRT1 directly regulates BDNF transcription by deacetylating and repressing Hes1, a transcriptional repressor of BDNF, thereby relieving inhibition and promoting neuronal survival. Directionally, SIRT1 deacetylates Hes1, which induces BDNF. This links sirtuin activity to neurotrophic support, and it is a mechanism for SIRT1's neuroprotective and cognitive benefits. By removing the Hes1 brake on the BDNF promoter, SIRT1 increases BDNF expression in the brain. This regulation is engaged by caloric restriction and exercise, both of which elevate BDNF through SIRT1-dependent pathways.

nodes.label: SIRT1/PGC-1α
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. Directionally, SIRT1/PGC-1α sits upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression, and it reinforces the metabolic-neurotrophic axis of SIRT1. By coordinating the activation of PGC-1α and the expression of BDNF, SIRT1 links mitochondrial function to neuronal survival and plasticity. This connection helps explain how sirtuin activation and caloric restriction benefit brain health.

nodes.label: BDNF promoter
nodes.description: SIRT1 activates PGC-1α, which co-activates the BDNF promoter, linking mitochondrial biogenesis to neurotrophic support. Directionally, SIRT1/PGC-1α sits upstream of BDNF transcription. This couples energy metabolism to neuronal growth-factor expression, and it reinforces the metabolic-neurotrophic axis of SIRT1. By coordinating the activation of PGC-1α and the expression of BDNF, SIRT1 links mitochondrial function to neuronal survival and plasticity. This connection helps explain how sirtuin activation and caloric restriction benefit brain health.

nodes.label: BDNF and NAD+ levels
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Exercise raises both BDNF and NAD+ levels, and SIRT1 may mediate exercise-induced BDNF upregulation in the hippocampus. Directionally, exercise sits upstream of BDNF and NAD+ elevation. Higher NAD+ fuels SIRT1, which then supports BDNF, and this provides a mechanistic bridge between physical activity, sirtuins, and brain health. By raising NAD+, exercise engages the sirtuin pathway that promotes BDNF expression and mitochondrial function. This axis is central to the well-established cognitive benefits of exercise and to the geroscience concept of exercise as medicine.

nodes.label: BDNF (via SIRT1/FoxO)
nodes.description: Caloric restriction and intermittent fasting elevate BDNF through SIRT1/FoxO-dependent pathways, contributing to cognitive resilience against aging. Directionally, caloric restriction sits upstream of BDNF elevation via SIRT1/FoxO. This neuroprotective adaptation complements CR's systemic benefits, and it motivates CR and fasting for brain health. By raising BDNF through sirtuin-dependent mechanisms, caloric restriction supports synaptic plasticity, neurogenesis, and neuronal survival. These effects contribute to the protection of cognitive function during aging.

nodes.label: PCAF
nodes.description: SIRT1 physically interacts with and deacetylates PCAF (p300/CBP-associated factor), a histone acetyltransferase, within regulatory complexes at muscle-gene promoters. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically inhibits PCAF. This counterbalances acetylation during myogenic regulation, and it shows SIRT1 tuning acetyltransferase partners, not only substrates. By deacetylating PCAF, SIRT1 reduces its HAT activity and its contribution to muscle-gene activation. This regulation is part of SIRT1's broader control of the acetylation-deacetylation balance that shapes transcriptional programs.

nodes.label: PCAF/GCN5
nodes.description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. Directionally, PCAF/GCN5 sits upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation, and SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD. By acetylating MyoD, these HATs support the expression of muscle-specific genes during differentiation. The balance between PCAF/GCN5 acetylation and sirtuin deacetylation determines the timing and extent of myogenic commitment.

nodes.label: MyoD
nodes.description: The positive histone acetyltransferases PCAF and GCN5 acetylate the myogenic transcription factor MyoD, enhancing its DNA-binding and recruitment of transcriptional machinery. Directionally, PCAF/GCN5 sits upstream of MyoD activation. This promotes muscle differentiation, and SIRT1 opposes this by deacetylating both PCAF and MyoD. By acetylating MyoD, these HATs support the expression of muscle-specific genes during differentiation. The balance between PCAF/GCN5 acetylation and sirtuin deacetylation determines the timing and extent of myogenic commitment.

nodes.label: MEF2D (at Lys424)
nodes.description: HDAC4 possesses SUMO E3 ligase activity and sumoylates MEF2D at Lys424, locking it into an inactive, transcription-repressing state. Directionally, HDAC4 sits upstream of MEF2D inactivation. This regulates muscle-gene expression independently of sirtuins, and it is included as a parallel chromatin regulatory mechanism contextualizing SIRT1's muscle actions. By sumoylating MEF2D, HDAC4 represses its transcriptional activity and the muscle genes it controls. This regulation is distinct from the acetylation-deacetylation balance that sirtuins influence, illustrating the diversity of muscle-gene control.

nodes.label: PML-IV
nodes.description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. Directionally, PML-IV sits upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision, and it connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression. By concentrating p53 and SIRT1 at nuclear bodies, PML-IV ensures that stress responses are locally integrated. This compartmentalization is central to the tumor-suppressive functions of the PML pathway.

nodes.label: p53 and SIRT1 to nuclear bodies
nodes.description: Upon oncogenic stress, the PML-IV isoform recruits both p53 and SIRT1 into PML nuclear bodies, assembling a stress-responsive regulatory hub. Directionally, PML-IV sits upstream of p53/SIRT1 compartmentalization. Within these bodies, SIRT1 deacetylates p53 to shape the senescence/apoptosis decision, and it connects PML bodies to sirtuin-mediated tumor suppression. By concentrating p53 and SIRT1 at nuclear bodies, PML-IV ensures that stress responses are locally integrated. nodes.norm_label: p53 and sirt1 to nuclear bodies

nodes.label: PML
nodes.description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. Directionally, PML sits upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies, and it contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest. By activating p53-dependent senescence, PML restricts uncontrolled proliferation and prevents tumor formation. The PML-SIRT1-p53 axis illustrates how a nuclear body can coordinate the decision between senescence, apoptosis, and proliferation.

nodes.label: Premature cellular senescence
nodes.description: PML-IV overexpression is sufficient to induce p53-dependent premature senescence, and loss of PML accelerates tumorigenesis, establishing PML as a tumor suppressor. Directionally, PML sits upstream of senescence. This process engages SIRT1 and p53 at PML nuclear bodies, and it contextualizes SIRT1's role in proliferation arrest. By activating p53-dependent senescence, PML restricts uncontrolled proliferation and prevents tumor formation. nodes.label: Mediterranean Diet
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways. Directionally, diet-derived resveratrol sits upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet, though human causality is inferential rather than proven. The Mediterranean Diet also provides other polyphenols and healthy fats that may act through SIRT1 and AMPK. This dietary association has motivated research into how whole-food polyphenol patterns, rather than isolated compounds, influence sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (via resveratrol)
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet's resveratrol content is proposed to activate SIRT1, linking the dietary pattern to longevity pathways. Directionally, diet-derived resveratrol sits upstream of SIRT1 activation. This is one of several polyphenol-mediated mechanisms of the diet, though human causality is inferential rather than proven. The Mediterranean Diet also provides other polyphenols and healthy fats that may act through SIRT1 and AMPK. This dietary association has motivated research into how whole-food polyphenol patterns, rather than isolated compounds, influence sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: Cardiovascular Disease risk
nodes.description: The PREDIMED trial showed that a Mediterranean diet supplemented with olive oil or nuts significantly reduced major cardiovascular events. Directionally, the dietary pattern sits upstream of lower CVD incidence. Polyphenols including resveratrol may engage SIRT1, but the effect is multifactorial, and it is a clinically validated dietary intervention. The trial provides the strongest evidence that a Mediterranean dietary pattern reduces cardiovascular risk. Its success supports the concept that whole-diet approaches, engaging multiple pathways including sirtuins, are effective for cardiovascular prevention.

nodes.label: Lipid profile (raises HDL, reduces LDL oxidation)
nodes.description: The Mediterranean Diet raises HDL while reducing LDL oxidation through its polyphenol-rich components, improving the overall lipid profile. Directionally, the diet sits upstream of favorable lipid changes. This contributes to its cardiovascular protection, and resveratrol and other polyphenols are putative SIRT1-engaging contributors. By combining healthy fats with antioxidant polyphenols, the diet improves both the quantity and quality of circulating lipoproteins. These lipid effects are part of the broader cardiovascular benefit demonstrated in clinical trials of the Mediterranean diet.
nodes.norm_label: lipid profile (raises hdl, reduces ldl oxidation)

nodes.label: SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio
nodes.description: The SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio defines the hormetic window—the dose range over which mitochondrial stress triggers adaptive responses rather than damage. Directionally, the ratio sits upstream of the adaptive-versus-harmful threshold. Because SIRT3 is protective and SIRT4 is detrimental, a high ratio broadens resilience, and caloric restriction and youth raise this ratio while aging lowers it. By setting the balance between mitochondrial protection and oxidant stress, the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio determines how cells respond to stress. Maintaining a high ratio is a proposed strategy for preserving mitochondrial health during aging.

nodes.label: SIRT3 (and downregulates SIRT4)
nodes.description: Caloric restriction upregulates SIRT3 and downregulates SIRT4, shifting the SIRT3/SIRT4 ratio toward a protective, oxidative-phosphorylation-promoting state. Directionally, caloric restriction sits upstream of the ratio shift. This counters the age-related pattern of declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4, and it is a core mechanism of CR's metabolic benefits. By biasing the balance toward SIRT3, caloric restriction promotes mitochondrial oxidation, antioxidant defense, and metabolic flexibility. This ratio shift is a key molecular readout of the beneficial effects of dietary restriction.

nodes.label: Declining SIRT3 and rising SIRT4
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Aging is associated with declining SIRT3 activity and rising SIRT4, which narrows the hormetic window and increases vulnerability to mitochondrial stressors. Directionally, aging sits upstream of the altered ratio. This shift favors oxidant stress and metabolic inflexibility, and restoring the ratio, for example via caloric restriction or NAD+ precursors, is a proposed anti-aging strategy. By reducing the protective SIRT3/SIRT4 balance, aging impairs mitochondrial quality control and stress adaptation. This association links mitochondrial sirtuin biology to the functional decline of aging tissues.

nodes.label: STACs
nodes.description: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide and NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. Directionally, STAC binding sits upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC, and it underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules. By increasing substrate affinity, STACs allow SIRT1 to deacetylate targets even at low NAD+ concentrations. This mechanism distinguishes true STACs from indirect NAD+-raising compounds, and it is central to STAC pharmacology.

nodes.label: SIRT1 KM for substrates
nodes.description: Sirtuin-activating compounds (STACs) such as resveratrol lower the Km of SIRT1 for its peptide and NAD+ substrates, amplifying deacetylation efficiency. Directionally, STAC binding sits upstream of enhanced catalytic rate. This allosteric effect is the defining action of a STAC, and it underlies the metabolic and longevity benefits attributed to these molecules. By increasing substrate affinity, STACs allow SIRT1 to deacetylate targets even at low NAD+ concentrations. This mechanism distinguishes true STACs from indirect NAD+-raising compounds, and it is central to STAC pharmacology.

nodes.label: NAD+ in tumor microenvironment
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins (overview, CD38 KO risks, cancer therapies).md
nodes.description: CD38 enzymatic activity depletes NAD+ in the tumor microenvironment and generates adenosine, suppressing anti-tumor T-cell and NK-cell responses. Directionally, CD38 sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and immunosuppression. This links CD38 to cancer immune evasion, and anti-CD38 antibodies both target myeloma and reshape the tumor microenvironment. By consuming NAD+ and producing immunosuppressive adenosine, CD38 on tumor and immune cells dampens anti-tumor immunity. This dual role makes CD38 both a therapeutic target and a mechanism of immune escape in cancer.

nodes.label: Anti-CD38 mAbs
nodes.description: Anti-CD38 monoclonal antibodies eliminate CD38+ Tregs and MDSCs and reduce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression, restoring T- and NK-cell function in the tumor microenvironment. Directionally, anti-CD38 therapy sits upstream of tumor-microenvironment reprogramming. This is both an anticancer action and a means to spare NAD+ for sirtuins, and it illustrates the dual therapeutic logic of CD38 targeting. By depleting immunosuppressive cells and reducing adenosine, these antibodies restore effector immune responses. The resulting reshaping of the tumor microenvironment contributes to the efficacy of anti-CD38 antibodies in multiple myeloma and other cancers.

nodes.label: FOXO3a (to induce BNIP3 mitophagy)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates FOXO3a, which transcriptionally induces BNIP3, forming the NAD+-SIRT1-FOXO3a-BNIP3 mitophagy axis that clears damaged mitochondria. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of BNIP3-dependent mitophagy. This protects cells from mitochondrial dysfunction and ROS, and it is a refined mitophagic branch of the SIRT1-FOXO3a program. By inducing BNIP3, FOXO3a promotes the selective removal of damaged mitochondria. This axis connects sirtuin-mediated NAD+ sensing to the quality control of the mitochondrial network.

nodes.label: HIF-2α
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates HIF-2α, modulating its stability and transcriptional output to influence metabolic adaptation to hypoxia. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically tunes HIF-2α. This parallels SIRT1's regulation of HIF-1α, and the evidence carries moderate confidence reflecting less-complete characterization of this substrate. By modifying HIF-2α, SIRT1 may influence the balance between the two hypoxia-inducible factors and their distinct target genes. This regulation is relevant to oxygen sensing, erythropoiesis, and the metabolic adaptation of cells to low-oxygen environments.

nodes.label: Retinoblastoma Protein (Rb)
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates the retinoblastoma protein (Rb) as part of its cell-cycle regulatory functions, influencing Rb's interaction with E2F and cell-cycle control. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically modifies Rb. This adds a cell-cycle dimension to SIRT1 beyond p53/E2F, and the evidence carries moderate confidence reflecting incomplete mechanistic detail. By deacetylating Rb, SIRT1 may modulate its ability to restrain E2F-dependent transcription and cell-cycle progression. This regulation connects SIRT1 to the G1/S checkpoint and to the control of proliferation in normal and cancer cells.

nodes.label: SIRT1/AMPK
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. Directionally, the interaction is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates LKB1 and PGC-1α while AMPK phosphorylates and activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit, and it is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance. By activating each other, SIRT1 and AMPK amplify catabolic and protective programs, including mitochondrial biogenesis and autophagy. This loop is a key target for interventions that aim to restore metabolic health in aging.

nodes.label: Energy homeostasis and autophagy
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and AMPK form a reciprocal regulatory loop in which each can activate the other, jointly promoting energy homeostasis and autophagic flux. Directionally, the interaction is bidirectional: SIRT1 deacetylates and activates LKB1 and PGC-1α while AMPK phosphorylates and activates SIRT1. This creates a self-reinforcing metabolic circuit, and it is a central node integrating nutrient sensing and clearance. By activating each other, SIRT1 and AMPK amplify catabolic and protective programs, including mitochondrial biogenesis and autophagy. This loop is a key target for interventions that aim to restore metabolic health in aging.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (Ser27, Thr344)
nodes.description: Under low-energy conditions, AMPK directly phosphorylates SIRT1 at Ser27 and Thr344, enhancing its deacetylase activity and coupling energy deficit to sirtuin function. Directionally, AMPK sits upstream of SIRT1 activation. This closes the reciprocal loop with SIRT1, and it ensures sirtuin responses track cellular AMP/ATP state. By phosphorylating SIRT1, AMPK links the energy-sensing kinase network to sirtuin-dependent gene regulation. This mechanism explains how fasting, exercise, and caloric restriction, which activate AMPK, also engage SIRT1-dependent programs.

nodes.label: p73
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates p73, suppressing its transcriptional activity and inhibiting apoptosis, analogous to its regulation of the related p53 family member. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatically inactivates p73. This promotes cell survival under stress but can be tumor-promoting, and it extends SIRT1's control over the p53 family. By deacetylating p73, SIRT1 dampens its ability to activate pro-apoptotic and cell-cycle-checkpoint genes. This regulation is relevant to both normal tissue protection and cancer, where p73 suppression by SIRT1 may reduce tumor-suppressive responses.

nodes.label: SIRT1 deacetylation of FOXO4
nodes.description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT1 activates FOXO4, which induces GADD45. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death, and it is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance. By inducing GADD45, FOXO4 supports nucleotide-excision repair and cell-cycle arrest, giving cells time to repair damage. This survival-oriented program is central to SIRT1's cytoprotective functions.

nodes.label: GADD45 expression
nodes.description: FOXO4 deacetylation by SIRT1 enhances expression of GADD45 and suppresses caspase-3/7 activity, promoting DNA repair over apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT1 activates FOXO4, which induces GADD45. This biases cells toward damage repair rather than death, and it is a further example of SIRT1 steering stress responses toward survival and genome maintenance. By inducing GADD45, FOXO4 supports nucleotide-excision repair and cell-cycle arrest, giving cells time to repair damage. This survival-oriented program is central to SIRT1's cytoprotective functions.

nodes.label: OX2R
nodes.description: In BRASTO mice, hypothalamic SIRT1 deacetylates the transcription factor NKX2-1, which drives expression of the orexin type 2 receptor (OX2R); increased OX2R in DMH/LH raises neural activity, physical activity, and energy expenditure, underpinning the approximately 11% lifespan extension. This positions the SIRT1-to-NKX2-1-to-OX2R pathway as a hypothalamic longevity axis that mimics calorie restriction. By increasing physical activity and energy expenditure through orexin signaling, SIRT1 promotes a CR-like metabolic state. This brain-centered mechanism demonstrates that sirtuin effects on lifespan can be mediated through neural control of energy balance.

nodes.label: NKX2-1
nodes.description: NKX2-1 (Nk2 homeobox 1) is deacetylated by SIRT1 in hypothalamic DMH/LH neurons; deacetylated NKX2-1 activates transcription of OX2R, the orexin receptor whose increased signaling recapitulates calorie restriction and extends lifespan in BRASTO mice. Thus NKX2-1 is the direct transcriptional relay between SIRT1 and OX2R. By linking SIRT1 activity to orexin-receptor expression, NKX2-1 connects sirtuin signaling to the neural circuits controlling arousal, activity, and energy expenditure. This pathway illustrates how a single transcription factor can mediate the longevity effects of sirtuin activation in the brain.

nodes.label: IGF-1 signaling
nodes.description: Male SIRT6 transgenics have lower serum IGF-1 and reduced downstream insulin/IGF-1-like signaling (AKT, pAKT); reduced insulin/IGF-1-like signaling is strongly associated with increased longevity in model organisms, providing the leading explanation for SIRT6's male-specific lifespan extension. Directionally, SIRT6-mediated inhibition of IGF-1 signaling sits upstream of lifespan extension. By suppressing the growth-promoting IGF-AKT axis, SIRT6 may recapitulate the longevity benefits of reduced insulin/IGF signaling. This mechanism connects SIRT6 to one of the most conserved longevity pathways across species.

nodes.label: CtIP
nodes.description: SIRT6 deacetylates CtIP (RBBP8), a key factor in DNA double-strand-break end resection and homologous recombination repair; this is one of the three best-characterized direct SIRT6 substrates (with H3K9ac/H3K56ac and GCN5) and links SIRT6 to genome stability and tumor suppression. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically modifies CtIP to support repair. By promoting end resection, CtIP enables homologous recombination, and its regulation by SIRT6 connects sirtuin activity to high-fidelity DNA repair. This substrate relationship is central to SIRT6's role in preventing genomic instability and cancer.

nodes.label: ADAM10
nodes.description: SIRT1 induces expression of ADAM10, the principal alpha-secretase that cleaves APP away from amyloidogenic beta-secretase (BACE1) processing, reducing beta-amyloid production; this underlies SIRT1's protective role in Alzheimer's disease models. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulates ADAM10 to promote non-amyloidogenic APP processing. By shifting APP cleavage away from the amyloidogenic pathway, SIRT1 reduces the production of toxic beta-amyloid peptides. This mechanism, together with SIRT1's anti-inflammatory and antioxidant actions, underlies its protection in Alzheimer's models and supports the idea that sirtuin activation could delay amyloid pathology.

nodes.label: IDH2
nodes.description: During dietary restriction, hepatic SIRT3 deacetylates and activates isocitrate dehydrogenase 2 (IDH2), increasing NADPH and regenerating glutathione to lower mitochondrial ROS; loss of SIRT3 abolishes this DR-dependent antioxidant response and exacerbates metabolic disease. Directionally, dietary restriction activates SIRT3, which activates IDH2. By boosting NADPH production and glutathione regeneration, this pathway protects mitochondria from oxidative damage during fasting. The dependence of this response on SIRT3 highlights the importance of mitochondrial sirtuins in mediating the metabolic benefits of dietary restriction.

nodes.label: Metabolic Syndrome
nodes.description: A nonsynonymous SIRT3 SNP reducing recombinant catalytic activity by about 34% is associated with metabolic syndrome in NAFLD patients and the Finnish Metabolic Syndrome in Men cohort, implicating lowered SIRT3 activity in human metabolic disease susceptibility. Directionally, reduced SIRT3 catalytic activity is associated with metabolic syndrome. This genetic evidence connects impaired mitochondrial sirtuin function to human metabolic disease, and it complements the animal studies showing that SIRT3 loss causes metabolic dysfunction. These findings support SIRT3 as a therapeutic target for metabolic syndrome.

nodes.label: Extrachromosomal rDNA Circles (ERCs)
nodes.description: Sir2p protects yeast from toxic accumulation of self-replicating extrachromosomal rDNA circles (ERCs); deletion of the replication-fork-blocking protein Fob1p rescues the short lifespan of sir2 mutants, establishing ERC suppression as the first mechanistic explanation for Sir2's longevity effect. Directionally, Sir2p suppresses ERC accumulation to extend lifespan. By preventing the toxic buildup of these circular DNA molecules, Sir2 preserves genome stability and replicative capacity. This was the first molecular mechanism linking Sir2 to longevity and remains a foundational finding in sirtuin research.

nodes.label: Mother cell
nodes.description: Sir2p maintains cellular polarity so that oxidized proteins, misfolded aggregates, and dysfunctional mitochondria are retained in the mother cell, allowing daughter cells to begin life undamaged; this asymmetric segregation extends daughter-cell lifespan at the mother's expense. Directionally, Sir2p promotes asymmetric segregation of damage to the mother cell. By ensuring that daughters are born free of damage, this mechanism supports the longevity of the lineage. It illustrates how sirtuins contribute to cellular rejuvenation, a concept that has influenced thinking about asymmetric cell division and aging.

nodes.label: Sas2p
nodes.description: A more recent epigenetic mechanism: Sir2p and the HAT Sas2p regulate H4K16 acetylation at the telomere-euchromatin boundary; Sir2p levels decline with age as H4K16Ac rises, and constitutive H4K16 acetylation shortens lifespan, linking subtelomeric silencing to yeast longevity. Directionally, the Sir2/Sas2 balance at telomeres determines lifespan. By maintaining H4K16 deacetylation at subtelomeric regions, Sir2 preserves the silenced state that supports longevity. This mechanism extends the sirtuin-longevity link beyond ERC suppression and highlights the importance of chromatin state in aging.

nodes.label: IRS-2
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates insulin receptor substrate-2 (IRS-2), a key adaptor in insulin and insulin-like growth factor signaling. This deacetylation enables efficient tyrosine phosphorylation of IRS-2 and downstream activation of the PI3K-Akt cascade, improving insulin signal transduction in peripheral tissues. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic activity sits upstream of enhanced insulin signaling. By reinforcing this pathway, SIRT1 helps counter insulin resistance and hyperglycemia in type 2 diabetes. The regulation illustrates how a single sirtuin can tune insulin sensitivity, and it positions SIRT1 activators as potential metabolic therapeutics alongside lifestyle interventions that raise NAD+.

nodes.label: CRTC2
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates CREB-regulated transcriptional coactivator 2 (CRTC2), an important regulator of hepatic gluconeogenesis. CRTC2 deacetylation occurs as part of SIRT1's dynamic, fasting-coupled control of glucose production in the liver, complementing its actions on FOXO1 and PGC-1alpha. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of CRTC2-dependent transcriptional programs. Together these branches fine-tune when and how much glucose the liver releases, balancing gluconeogenic output against the body's energy needs. The coordination of CRTC2, FOXO1 and PGC-1alpha shows that SIRT1 integrates multiple transcriptional nodes to achieve homeostatic glucose control during fasting and refeeding.

nodes.label: Akt phosphorylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 negatively regulates the insulin-signaling cascade by suppressing upstream signaling through the insulin receptor and insulin receptor substrates. This restraint reduces downstream Akt phosphorylation, preventing excessive glucose uptake and helping to maintain metabolic balance in peripheral tissues. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of dampened insulin-PI3K-Akt signaling. Loss of SIRT6 elevates this signaling, contributing to insulin resistance and metabolic dysfunction. By toning down insulin-driven anabolic responses, SIRT6 protects cells from nutrient overload and supports the metabolic flexibility that is lost in obesity and type 2 diabetes.

nodes.label: SREBP2
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 limits cholesterol and lipid accumulation in the liver by repressing the sterol-regulatory transcription factor SREBP2. Suppression of SREBP2 restrains the expression of cholesterol-biosynthetic genes, contributing to SIRT6's protection against hepatic steatosis and systemic metabolic dysfunction. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of SREBP2-dependent cholesterol synthesis. This complements SIRT6's repression of SREBP-1c-mediated fatty-acid synthesis, giving SIRT6 broad control over hepatic lipid homeostasis.

nodes.label: ATGL
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 enhances adipose tissue lipolysis and prevents lipotoxic insulin resistance by inducing expression of adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL), the rate-limiting enzyme of triglyceride breakdown. This induction is dependent on the transcription factor FOXO1, which SIRT6 engages to drive ATGL gene expression. Directionally, SIRT6 promotes fat mobilization through FOXO1-dependent ATGL induction. By mobilizing stored fat, this pathway supplies fuel during fasting and prevents the accumulation of lipid intermediates that impair insulin signaling. The regulation supports SIRT6's role in metabolic flexibility, balancing lipid storage against oxidation according to systemic energy demands.

nodes.label: XBP1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 alleviates endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress by regulating the transcription factor XBP1, a central mediator of the unfolded-protein response. By modulating XBP1, SIRT6 limits the inflammatory and metabolic dysfunction that arises from chronic ER stress in the liver. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of XBP1-dependent stress resolution. This action complements SIRT6's H3K9 deacetylation at glycolytic gene promoters, giving it coordinated control over hepatic metabolism and stress signaling. In this way SIRT6 couples chromatin regulation to the unfolded-protein response, protecting hepatocytes from the damage that drives fatty liver disease and metabolic decline.

nodes.label: PCSK9
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 regulates systemic lipid homeostasis in part through PCSK9, a secreted protein that controls LDL receptor degradation and thereby plasma LDL-cholesterol levels. Deficiency of SIRT6 accelerates atherosclerosis through dysregulation of PCSK9 and impaired LDL metabolism, indicating that SIRT6 normally constrains PCSK9-driven LDL accumulation. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of PCSK9 and LDL handling. By restraining this axis, SIRT6 limits the lipid burden on the vascular wall and protects against atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. This places SIRT6 among the chromatin-regulatory proteins that influence cardiovascular risk through systemic cholesterol control.

nodes.label: GABPβ1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 deacetylates GA-binding protein beta1 (GABPbeta1), a subunit of the GABP transcription factor complex that controls expression of nuclear-encoded mitochondrial genes. Deacetylation facilitates GABP complex formation and transcriptional activation of these genes, supporting mitochondrial biogenesis and function. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of GABP-dependent mitochondrial gene expression. SIRT7 deficiency accordingly causes systemic mitochondrial dysfunction, manifesting as lactate accumulation and cardiac abnormalities.

nodes.label: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: Beyond its well-known mono-ADP-ribosylation of glutamate dehydrogenase, SIRT4 also functions as a lipoamidase that regulates the pyruvate dehydrogenase complex. By removing lipoate modifications, SIRT4 can influence pyruvate dehydrogenase activity and thereby control entry of glucose-derived carbon into the tricarboxylic acid cycle. Directionally, SIRT4's lipoamidase activity sits upstream of pyruvate dehydrogenase regulation. This broadens SIRT4's control of mitochondrial substrate oxidation and adds to its role in metabolic flexibility.

nodes.label: NNMT
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: Nicotinamide N-methyltransferase (NNMT) methylates nicotinamide to 1-methylnicotinamide, diverting this precursor away from the NAMPT-dependent salvage pathway. By withdrawing nicotinamide from NAD+ regeneration, NNMT activity limits NAD+ biosynthesis and indirectly modulates the activity of NAD+-dependent sirtuins. Directionally, NNMT sits upstream of reduced NAD+ availability. This makes NNMT a metabolic competitor with the salvage pathway, and elevated NNMT in obesity and certain cancers contributes to NAD+ depletion and metabolic dysfunction. Modulating NNMT is therefore of interest as a strategy to preserve NAD+ pools and support sirtuin activity in disease states.

nodes.label: Brown Adipose Tissue
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 supports thermogenesis in brown and beige adipose tissue, which is induced under cold exposure, thereby contributing to energy expenditure and protection from obesity. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of thermogenic gene programs in brown adipose tissue. This pro-thermogenic role opposes SIRT7, which suppresses brown-adipose function, illustrating opposing actions within the sirtuin family on energy expenditure. By maintaining the capacity of brown and beige fat to burn calories, SIRT6 helps the body dissipate energy as heat rather than store it. Supporting SIRT6 activity is therefore considered a potential approach for counteracting weight gain and metabolic disease.

nodes.label: UCP1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 controls thermogenesis in brown adipose tissue by deacetylating regulatory targets upstream of the uncoupling protein UCP1, maintaining the mitochondrial function required for adaptive heat production. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of UCP1-dependent thermogenic capacity. By preserving mitochondrial oxidative function and reducing oxidative stress in brown fat, SIRT3 ensures that mitochondria can sustain the proton leak through UCP1 that generates heat. This makes SIRT3 important for cold-induced thermogenesis and overall energy balance.

nodes.label: mTOR signaling
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: Nutrient abundance activates the mTOR pathway, which promotes anabolic processes such as protein synthesis and lipid accumulation while suppressing autophagy. Sirtuins counterbalance this anabolic state by favoring catabolic pathways that restore metabolic equilibrium. Directionally, sirtuins and mTOR act as opposed nutrient-sensing axes. This opposition is most evident during caloric restriction or fasting, when falling nutrient signals dampen mTOR while NAD+-sensitive sirtuins drive fatty-acid oxidation, mitochondrial maintenance, and autophagy.

nodes.label: WAT browning
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates PPARgamma at lysine residues K268 and K293, and this modification promotes exchange of cofactors within the PPARgamma transcriptional complex. The resulting change in cofactor recruitment enhances browning of white adipose tissue, increasing thermogenesis, mitochondrial biogenesis, and PGC-1alpha-dependent oxidative programs. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic modification of PPARgamma sits upstream of beige adipocyte induction. Because PPARgamma is a master regulator of adipocyte biology, its deacetylation by SIRT1 can shift adipose tissue from a fat-storing toward a fat-burning phenotype.

nodes.label: FoxO1 deacetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 suppresses adipocyte differentiation through deacetylation of the transcription factor FoxO1, which reinforces FoxO1-mediated repression of PPARgamma. Consistent with this, reduced SIRT1 and SIRT2 expression in visceral adipose stem cells from obese individuals correlates with enhanced adipogenic capacity and visceral fat expansion. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of FoxO1-dependent anti-adipogenic programs. By keeping FoxO1 active in repressing PPARgamma, SIRT2 restrains the conversion of precursor cells into mature adipocytes.

nodes.label: LCAD (fatty acid β-oxidation)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: Fasting induces SIRT3 activation, which in turn enhances fatty acid oxidation through deacetylation and activation of long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD), a key enzyme of mitochondrial beta-oxidation. Directionally, SIRT3 enzymatic activation of LCAD sits upstream of enhanced lipid catabolism. This promotes the harvest of energy from fat stores during fasting and caloric restriction, when glucose is scarce. By supporting efficient beta-oxidation, SIRT3 helps maintain ATP production while limiting the accumulation of damaging lipid intermediates.

nodes.label: Pyruvate Dehydrogenase (PDH)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 maintains the activity of pyruvate dehydrogenase (PDH) by preventing its hyperacetylation, thereby coupling glycolysis-derived carbon to mitochondrial oxidation. Loss of SIRT3 leads to PDH hyperacetylation, reduced glucose oxidation, and accumulation of pyruvate and lactate, impairing metabolic flexibility in skeletal muscle. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of PDH-dependent glucose oxidation. By protecting PDH, SIRT3 ensures that glucose can be oxidized in mitochondria rather than being diverted to lactate, preserving energy efficiency during exercise and metabolic stress. This function is central to SIRT3's role in supporting muscle performance and whole-body glucose handling.

nodes.label: Malonyl-CoA decarboxylase
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: In hepatocytes, SIRT4 represses PPARalpha signaling and inhibits malonyl-CoA decarboxylase, shifting liver metabolism away from mitochondrial fatty-acid utilization and toward anabolic lipid conservation. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of suppressed fatty acid oxidation. This metabolic brake counterbalances SIRT3, which promotes beta-oxidation, so the relative activity of the two mitochondrial sirtuins determines whether the liver oxidizes or stores fat. Under chronic nutrient surplus, sustained SIRT4 activity contributes to hepatic steatosis, whereas conditions that shift the SIRT3/SIRT4 balance toward SIRT3 favor fat burning.

nodes.label: VLCAD, LCAD, MCAD, ECHA (fatty acid oxidation)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 activates multiple fatty acid beta-oxidation enzymes through desuccinylation, including very-long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (VLCAD), long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (LCAD), medium-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (MCAD), and the alpha subunit of enoyl-CoA hydratase (ECHA). Directionally, SIRT5 enzymatic activation of these enzymes sits upstream of enhanced lipid catabolism. Deficiency of SIRT5 compromises fatty acid metabolism, leading to acylcarnitine accumulation and decreased ATP production.
nodes.norm_label: vlcad, lcad, mcad, echa (fatty acid oxidation)

nodes.label: Telomeric chromatin
nodes.source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
nodes.description: SIRT1's histone deacetylase activity is directly associated with regulation of telomeric chromatin, gene expression, and the dynamic association of DNA repair factors with chromatin. Telomere shortening occurs over the lifespan and has been linked to the concomitant decrease in SIRT1 expression with age. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of telomeric chromatin maintenance. By preserving the integrity of telomere-associated chromatin and facilitating repair factor access, SIRT1 helps stabilize the chromosome ends whose erosion is a hallmark of aging.

nodes.label: 40 substrates
nodes.source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 functions as a deacetylase that modulates more than forty known substrates involved in inflammation, stress resistance, mitochondrial biogenesis, fatty acid metabolism, insulin secretion, glucose production, and lipid homeostasis. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic activity sits upstream of a broad network of cellular processes. This extraordinary substrate diversity explains why SIRT1 participates in metabolism, stress resistance, inflammation, and longevity across many tissues. The wide substrate range also means SIRT1's effects are highly context-dependent, with outcomes shaped by the tissue, the nutrient state, and the specific substrates engaged.

nodes.label: N-Myc and c-Myc
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 enhances the protein stability of the oncogenic transcription factors N-Myc and c-Myc, promoting cancer cell proliferation. This represents an oncogenic function of SIRT2 that is distinct from its tumor-suppressive roles in other cellular contexts. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Myc stabilization and enhanced proliferation. By protecting these potent oncogenes from degradation, SIRT2 can support the growth of Myc-driven tumors, complicating the simple view of sirtuins as universal tumor suppressors.

nodes.label: AKR1C1 (inhibiting STAT3 transactivation)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 deacetylates aldo-keto reductase family 1 member C1 (AKR1C1), and this modification inhibits transactivation of STAT3 target genes, suppressing migration of non-small-cell lung cancer cells both in vitro and in xenograft models. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of AKR1C1 sits upstream of reduced STAT3-driven metastasis. By restraining STAT3 transcriptional activity, SIRT2 limits the invasive and migratory phenotype that contributes to lung cancer progression. This tumor-suppressive axis contrasts with SIRT2's pro-tumorigenic stabilization of Myc in other settings, reinforcing the context-dependence of sirtuin biology in oncology.

nodes.label: IDH1 (repressing CRC migration)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: In human colorectal cancer, SIRT2-dependent deacetylation of the metabolic enzyme IDH1 represses cancer cell migration and invasion both in vitro and in vivo. This regulation of IDH1 influences cellular metabolism and inhibits the formation of liver metastases. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of IDH1 sits upstream of suppressed colorectal cancer metastasis. By modulating IDH1 and the metabolic state of the tumor cell, SIRT2 limits the invasive capacity that drives metastatic spread. This positions SIRT2 as a suppressor of colorectal cancer progression and indicates that preserving SIRT2 activity, or mimicking its effects, could restrain metastasis in this malignancy.

nodes.label: E-cadherin promotion
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 suppresses epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) by promoting expression of the epithelial marker E-cadherin in gastric cancer cells. This maintains an epithelial phenotype and inhibits cancer cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of maintained epithelial phenotype and suppressed metastasis. By preventing the loss of E-cadherin that characterizes EMT, SIRT4 blocks a key step in the acquisition of invasive and migratory behavior. This supports SIRT4's role as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer, where its downregulation may allow tumors to progress toward metastatic disease.

nodes.label: Snail-dependent KLF4 repression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 drives epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) and metastasis in non-small-cell lung cancer through Snail-dependent transrepression of the transcription factor KLF4. This represents an oncogenic function of SIRT6 that contrasts sharply with its tumor-suppressive roles in other cancers. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of EMT induction and metastatic progression in this context. By repressing KLF4, an epithelial-fate factor, SIRT6 allows Snail to drive the mesenchymal program that promotes invasion and spread.

nodes.label: BRCA1 deacetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 promotes BRCA1-BARD1 heterodimerization through deacetylation of BRCA1, facilitating assembly of the repair complex required for homologous recombination. This supports genome maintenance and tumor suppression by enabling high-fidelity repair of DNA double-strand breaks. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic licensing of BRCA1 sits upstream of repair complex formation. By promoting homologous recombination, SIRT2 helps cells repair potentially oncogenic DNA damage accurately rather than through error-prone pathways. This links SIRT2 to DNA repair fidelity and explains part of its tumor-suppressive activity.

nodes.label: Slug (EMT transcription factor)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: In basal-like breast cancer, SIRT2 maintains the protein stability of Slug, an epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition (EMT) transcription factor, through deacetylation. Stabilized Slug contributes to the robust tumorigenic activity of basal-like breast cancer, along with its enhanced invasive and metastatic capabilities. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Slug-dependent EMT and tumor progression. By protecting Slug from degradation, SIRT2 sustains the mesenchymal program that drives invasion and metastasis in this aggressive breast cancer subtype.

nodes.label: SIRT1 (via glutamine metabolism)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 exerts tumor-suppressive activity in breast cancer by negatively regulating expression of SIRT1, and this suppression occurs through repression of glutamine metabolism. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of reduced SIRT1 expression via metabolic regulation. This reveals cross-talk between mitochondrial and nuclear sirtuin proteins in cancer progression, where mitochondrial SIRT4 restrains nuclear SIRT1-dependent growth programs. By limiting glutamine utilization and, consequently, SIRT1 levels, SIRT4 curbs the metabolic and survival advantages that SIRT1 confers on tumor cells.

nodes.label: FoxO1/MDR2 upregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 causes tamoxifen resistance in ER-alpha-positive breast cancer cells through upregulation of multidrug resistance protein 2 (MDR2), an effect mediated by deacetylation of the transcription factor FoxO1. Inhibition of SIRT1 impairs nuclear FoxO1 accumulation and MDR2 expression and augments the cytotoxic effects of paclitaxel and doxorubicin in tamoxifen-resistant cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of FoxO1- and MDR2-mediated chemoresistance. By driving drug-efflux capacity in resistant cells, SIRT1 reduces the efficacy of endocrine therapy and other agents.

nodes.label: VEGF-A elevation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 promotes cisplatin resistance in non-small-cell lung cancer cells by elevating expression of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A). SIRT1 is upregulated in cisplatin-resistant tumor tissues and cells compared with cisplatin-sensitive groups, correlating with the resistant phenotype. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of VEGF-A-mediated chemoresistance. By enhancing VEGF-A, SIRT1 may support tumor survival and adaptive responses that blunt the cytotoxic effects of cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential target for overcoming chemotherapy resistance in lung cancer, since inhibiting SIRT1 could lower VEGF-A and re-sensitize resistant tumors to platinum-based treatment.

nodes.label: ATM-Chk2 DNA damage repair
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 promotes DNA damage repair and radioresistance through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM)-Chk2 pathway in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. By supporting this DNA-damage-response branch, SIRT3 enables cancer cells to survive ionizing radiation more effectively. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair and radiation resistance. This has therapeutic implications, because combining SIRT3 inhibition with radiotherapy could impair the repair of radiation-induced damage and thereby improve treatment efficacy.

nodes.label: p16 and p21
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 upregulates expression of the cell-cycle inhibitor genes p16 and p21, while suppressing CyclinB1/Cdc2 and Cdc25c, and this cell-cycle blockade induces apoptosis in hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest and apoptosis induction. By enforcing these checkpoints, SIRT4 functions as a tumor suppressor in liver cancer, limiting proliferation and promoting death of transformed cells. The coordinated upregulation of p16 and p21 with suppression of cell-cycle drivers reflects SIRT4's broad influence on the machinery that governs entry into mitosis. This supports interest in SIRT4 as a therapeutic target for hepatocellular carcinoma.

nodes.label: Glutathione S-transferase π1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 downregulates both the mRNA and protein levels of glutathione S-transferase pi 1 (GSTP1), a phase II detoxification enzyme involved in the metabolism of chemotherapeutic agents. SIRT3 overexpression promotes sorafenib-induced apoptosis and thereby enhances the drug sensitivity of hepatocellular carcinoma cells. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced GSTP1 and enhanced drug responsiveness. By lowering the capacity of cancer cells to detoxify sorafenib, SIRT3 restores sensitivity to this agent. This suggests that SIRT3 expression status could predict sorafenib response in liver cancer, and that boosting SIRT3 may help overcome drug resistance in this malignancy.

nodes.label: JAK2/STAT3 inhibition
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 suppresses hepatocellular carcinoma cell growth through induction of apoptosis, inhibition of oxidative stress, and blockade of the JAK2/STAT3 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade and tumor suppression. By restraining this oncogenic signaling axis, SIRT6 limits the proliferative and survival signals that drive liver cancer progression. The combination of apoptosis induction and oxidative-stress suppression reflects SIRT6's multi-pronged tumor-suppressive activity. This positions SIRT6 as a promising target for hepatocellular carcinoma, where restoring or enhancing SIRT6 function could complement existing treatments.

nodes.label: eNOS activation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Endothelial-cell-specific overexpression of SIRT1 protects against atherosclerosis in apolipoprotein E-deficient mice, and this protection is associated with inhibition of endothelial cell apoptosis through activation of eNOS expression. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of eNOS-dependent vascular protection. By maintaining nitric oxide production and limiting endothelial cell death, SIRT1 preserves endothelial function and resists the progression of atherosclerotic lesions. This positions SIRT1 as an atheroprotective factor in the vasculature and supports efforts to activate SIRT1 as a strategy against cardiovascular disease.

nodes.label: Macrophage polarization
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 decreases atherosclerotic plaque formation in LDL receptor-deficient mice by regulating macrophage polarization. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of anti-atherogenic macrophage phenotypes. By steering macrophages toward less inflammatory states, SIRT2 reduces the foam-cell accumulation and chronic inflammation that drive plaque development. This links SIRT2 to innate immune modulation in vascular disease, complementing the anti-inflammatory actions of other sirtuins. Because macrophages are central to atherosclerosis, interventions that preserve SIRT2 activity in these cells could help limit plaque burden and stabilize existing lesions, reducing the risk of cardiovascular events.

nodes.label: COPD development
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Reduced SIRT6 expression is associated with COPD development through enhancement of cellular senescence that arises from insufficient autophagy during cigarette smoke exposure. SIRT6 deficiency impairs autophagy and promotes premature senescence in lung cells. Directionally, SIRT6 deficiency sits upstream of impaired autophagy and accelerated cellular aging in the lung. By failing to clear damaged components, cells accumulate and enter senescence, contributing to the structural remodeling and functional decline characteristic of COPD.

nodes.label: SIRT3 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 deficiency in the aging murine lung promotes a fibrotic response mediated by TGF-beta1 and augments mitochondrial DNA damage and apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. Conversely, SIRT3 overexpression can ameliorate asbestos-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Directionally, SIRT3 deficiency sits upstream of enhanced TGF-beta1-driven fibrosis, because by weakening mitochondrial antioxidant defenses it renders alveolar epithelial cells vulnerable to the damage that fuels the fibrotic program. Restoring SIRT3 could therefore protect against pulmonary fibrosis, making mitochondrial sirtuin activity an important determinant of lung resilience to environmental and aging-related fibrotic injury.

nodes.label: Lung fibrosis via TGF-β1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 deficiency in the aging murine lung promotes a fibrotic response mediated by TGF-beta1 and augments mitochondrial DNA damage and apoptosis in alveolar epithelial cells. Conversely, SIRT3 overexpression can ameliorate asbestos-induced pulmonary fibrosis. Directionally, SIRT3 deficiency sits upstream of enhanced TGF-beta1-driven fibrosis, because by weakening mitochondrial antioxidant defenses it renders alveolar epithelial cells vulnerable to the damage that fuels the fibrotic program. Restoring SIRT3 could therefore protect against pulmonary fibrosis, making mitochondrial sirtuin activity an important determinant of lung resilience to environmental and aging-related fibrotic injury.

nodes.label: Th2 responses and macrophage polarization
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 enhances allergic asthmatic inflammation by upregulating T-helper type 2 responses and macrophage polarization. Pharmacologic ablation of SIRT2 attenuates, while genetic SIRT2 overexpression exaggerates, the allergic asthmatic phenotype. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of Th2-driven allergic inflammation. By promoting the type 2 immune response characteristic of asthma, SIRT2 amplifies airway inflammation and the associated pathology. This makes SIRT2 inhibition a candidate therapeutic approach for allergic asthma, since reducing SIRT2 activity could dampen Th2 responses and macrophage-mediated inflammation, providing a potential strategy to modulate the severity of the disease.

nodes.label: Unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis may impact lymphocyte homeostasis in COVID-19 patients. COVID-19 is characterized by increased p53 transcription in circulating lymphocytes and a persistently activated form of p53, possibly due to low SIRT1 levels. Directionally, low SIRT1 and elevated p53 activity sit upstream of disturbed lymphocyte homeostasis. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates p53 and restrains its pro-apoptotic activity, its deficiency could leave lymphocytes vulnerable to p53-driven apoptosis and contribute to the lymphopenia seen in severe disease. Increased SIRT1 expression might therefore help alleviate COVID-19 pathogenesis by restoring the balance of this axis.

nodes.label: COVID-19 lymphocyte homeostasis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The unbalanced p53/SIRT1 axis may impact lymphocyte homeostasis in COVID-19 patients. COVID-19 is characterized by increased p53 transcription in circulating lymphocytes and a persistently activated form of p53, possibly due to low SIRT1 levels. Directionally, low SIRT1 and elevated p53 activity sit upstream of disturbed lymphocyte homeostasis. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates p53 and restrains its pro-apoptotic activity, its deficiency could leave lymphocytes vulnerable to p53-driven apoptosis and contribute to the lymphopenia seen in severe disease. Increased SIRT1 expression might therefore help alleviate COVID-19 pathogenesis by restoring the balance of this axis.

nodes.label: SIRT3 levels
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Serum SIRT3 levels are markedly lower in severe COVID-19 patients compared with those with mild or moderate disease, indicating a positive role of SIRT3 in alleviating COVID-19. Directionally, SIRT3 levels sit upstream of clinical outcome and prognosis. Because SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense and dampens inflammation, its reduction in severe cases may permit greater oxidative stress and inflammatory damage. SIRT3 levels therefore serve as an indicator of disease severity and associate with prognosis.

nodes.label: COVID-19 clinical outcome
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Serum SIRT3 levels are markedly lower in severe COVID-19 patients compared with those with mild or moderate disease, indicating a positive role of SIRT3 in alleviating COVID-19. Directionally, SIRT3 levels sit upstream of clinical outcome and prognosis. Because SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense and dampens inflammation, its reduction in severe cases may permit greater oxidative stress and inflammatory damage. SIRT3 levels therefore serve as an indicator of disease severity and associate with prognosis.

nodes.label: Metabolic switch in cardiac hypertrophy
nodes.description: SIRT1 interacts with and activates PPARalpha to prevent the metabolic switch from fatty acid oxidation to glycolysis that occurs in cardiac hypertrophy. By promoting fatty acid oxidation gene expression and inactivating NF-kappaB, SIRT1 preserves the adult heart's preferred fuel preference. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of PPARalpha-dependent metabolic preservation. Maintaining fatty acid oxidation prevents the maladaptive glycolytic shift that accompanies hypertrophic growth and heart failure.

nodes.label: SOD2 and Catalase
nodes.description: SIRT3 protects against cardiac hypertrophy by inducing expression of the antioxidant proteins SOD2 and catalase. The SIRT3-mediated reduction in reactive oxygen species inhibits AKT signaling and the downstream gene expression associated with hypertrophy induction. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of antioxidant defense and hypertrophy suppression, since by lowering mitochondrial oxidative stress it removes a key stimulus for the growth signaling that drives pathological cardiac enlargement. This places mitochondrial sirtuin activity at the center of the redox control governing cardiac stress responses.

nodes.label: c-Jun (cardiac hypertrophy)
nodes.description: SIRT6 functions as a negative regulator of cardiac hypertrophy by co-repressing c-Jun-dependent transcription at the chromatin level, thereby inhibiting downstream IGF-AKT signaling. In vivo inhibition of IGF signaling in SIRT6 knockout mice abrogates the hypertrophic response. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed c-Jun transcription and IGF-AKT signaling. By restraining this growth-promoting axis, SIRT6 limits the pathological growth signals that drive cardiac hypertrophy. The observation that blocking IGF signaling rescues the hypertrophic phenotype confirms that this pathway mediates the effect.

nodes.label: SIRT3 gene
nodes.description: The human SIRT3 gene is deleted in up to 20% of all human cancers analyzed overall, and in up to 40% of breast and ovarian cancers. This frequent deletion establishes SIRT3 as a tumor suppressor that acts through reactive oxygen species suppression and metabolic regulation. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of increased tumorigenesis susceptibility. By removing mitochondrial antioxidant protection, deletion of SIRT3 raises oxidative stress that can drive oncogenic signaling and genomic damage. The high deletion frequency, especially in breast and ovarian cancer, suggests SIRT3 status is an important determinant of cancer risk and may have prognostic value.

nodes.label: 20% of human cancers
nodes.description: The human SIRT3 gene is deleted in up to 20% of all human cancers analyzed overall, and in up to 40% of breast and ovarian cancers. This frequent deletion establishes SIRT3 as a tumor suppressor that acts through reactive oxygen species suppression and metabolic regulation. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of increased tumorigenesis susceptibility. By removing mitochondrial antioxidant protection, deletion of SIRT3 raises oxidative stress that can drive oncogenic signaling and genomic damage. The high deletion frequency, especially in breast and ovarian cancer, suggests SIRT3 status is an important determinant of cancer risk and may have prognostic value.

nodes.label: SIRT6 locus
nodes.description: A survey of approximately one thousand human cancer cell lines revealed that the SIRT6 locus was deleted in 35% of the samples. This high deletion frequency supports SIRT6's role as a tumor suppressor that acts through repression of HIF-1alpha and c-MYC and suppression of glycolytic metabolic reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of enhanced oncogenic metabolism and tumor growth. Without SIRT6, the brakes on aerobic glycolysis and proliferation are released, promoting the metabolic phenotype that sustains cancer. The prevalence of SIRT6 deletion across diverse cancer cell lines underscores its broad importance in restraining malignancy.

nodes.label: 35% of cancer cell lines
nodes.description: A survey of approximately one thousand human cancer cell lines revealed that the SIRT6 locus was deleted in 35% of the samples. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of enhanced oncogenic metabolism and tumor growth. Without SIRT6, the brakes on aerobic glycolysis and proliferation are released, promoting the metabolic phenotype that sustains cancer. The prevalence of SIRT6 deletion across diverse cancer cell lines underscores its broad importance in restraining malignancy.

nodes.label: ATM-p53/p73 pathway
nodes.description: Ectopic SIRT6 overexpression results in increased p53- and p73-dependent apoptosis through the ataxia telangiectasia mutated (ATM) kinase, and this effect requires SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of ATM-dependent activation of p53 and p73. This reveals a deacetylation-independent tumor-suppressive mechanism of SIRT6, in which its enzymatic transfer of ADP-ribose rather than histone deacetylation triggers the cell-death program. By engaging the p53 family, SIRT6 can eliminate stressed or transformed cells before they become established tumors. This expands our understanding of sirtuin catalytic diversity in cancer suppression.

nodes.label: Aging (depleting NAD+)
nodes.description: CD38, the major NADase in many mouse tissues, increases with age and depletes cellular NAD+ pools, thereby compromising sirtuin function. Mice lacking CD38 show elevated NAD+ levels and increased SIRT1 activity, coupled with protection from diet-induced obesity. Directionally, age-related CD38 upregulation sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and reduced sirtuin activity. Because sirtuins depend on NAD+ as a co-substrate, the rising NAD+ consumption by CD38 during aging starves sirtuin enzymes of their fuel. This makes CD38 a key target for NAD+-restoring interventions, and CD38 inhibition is being explored as a way to preserve NAD+ and support sirtuin function during aging.

nodes.label: PARP1 and PARP2
nodes.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
nodes.description: PARP1 and PARP2 are major NAD+-consuming enzymes whose activity can deplete cellular NAD+ pools and compromise sirtuin function, creating competition for the same limited co-substrate. Directionally, PARP activity sits upstream of NAD+ consumption and reduced sirtuin availability. This competition is especially relevant during DNA damage, when PARP activation surges and rapidly consumes NAD+ to synthesize ADP-ribose polymers. Because both PARPs and sirtuins are essential for genome maintenance and stress responses, their shared dependence on NAD+ creates an intrinsic trade-off.

nodes.label: NAMPT/NAD+ cycle
nodes.source_file: _document_ - SIRT1 Protein roles at the nexus of health, disease, and therapeutics.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 deacetylates PGC-1alpha and amplifies expression of the circadian transcription factors BMAL1 and CLOCK. A key target of the BMAL1-CLOCK complex is NAMPT, establishing a circadian NAD+ biosynthesis cycle that rhythmically activates and deactivates SIRT1 in alignment with the daily cycle. Directionally, the NAMPT-NAD+ cycle sits upstream of rhythmic SIRT1 activity. Because SIRT1 feeds back to regulate clock components, this forms a stable oscillator coupling metabolism to circadian time. Disruption of this loop, as seen with aging and shift work, impairs both circadian function and metabolic health.

nodes.label: CHD4 (chromatin remodeler)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 can coordinate with the chromatin remodeler chromodomain-helicase-DNA-binding 4 (CHD4) to promote chromatin relaxation and DNA repair, exerting an anticarcinogenic role in lung cancer. Directionally, SIRT6 and CHD4 cooperation sits upstream of enhanced DNA repair capacity. By opening chromatin at sites of damage, the pair facilitates access of repair machinery and promotes accurate repair of DNA lesions. This reduces the genomic instability that drives cancer initiation and progression. The finding highlights how sirtuins partner with chromatin remodelers to maintain genome integrity, and it supports SIRT6 as a relevant target in lung cancer prevention and therapy.

nodes.label: SIRT6 silencing
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 silencing can overcome sorafenib resistance by promoting ferroptosis in gastric cancer, suggesting a therapeutic strategy for resistant malignancies. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of ferroptotic cell death and restored drug sensitivity. By triggering this iron-dependent form of cell death, SIRT6 depletion bypasses the resistance mechanisms that allow gastric cancer cells to survive sorafenib treatment. This reveals an unexpected pro-survival role for SIRT6 in this context, where its activity protects cells from ferroptosis.

nodes.label: Twist downregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 overexpression dramatically suppresses the metastatic capability of ovarian cancer cells by inhibiting epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition through downregulation of Twist, a key EMT transcription factor. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of Twist suppression and maintenance of an epithelial phenotype. By reducing Twist, SIRT3 blocks the switch that confers migratory and invasive behavior on tumor cells. This restrains the metastatic spread that is the main cause of ovarian cancer mortality. The finding positions SIRT3 as a suppressor of ovarian cancer metastasis and suggests that maintaining SIRT3 activity could help limit disease dissemination.

nodes.label: Nrf2/HO-1 pathway (ovarian cancer)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 promotes cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by suppressing DNA damage in a ROS-dependent manner through regulation of the Nrf2/Heme Oxygenase-1 pathway. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of Nrf2-mediated chemoresistance. By activating this antioxidant program, SIRT5 helps cancer cells neutralize the reactive oxygen species that contribute to cisplatin-induced DNA damage. This reduces the genotoxic burden of the drug and blunts its cytotoxicity, allowing tumor cells to survive treatment. Inhibiting SIRT5, therefore, could re-sensitize ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin by dismantling their antioxidant defenses.

nodes.label: SIRT1-mediated PAK1 deacetylation at K420
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) at lysine 420 hinders autophagy and glioblastoma growth, establishing SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic inhibition of PAK1 sits upstream of suppressed glioblastoma progression. By restraining PAK1 activity, SIRT1 limits the autophagy that glioblastoma cells rely on to survive under metabolic stress. This impairs tumor growth and positions SIRT1 as a brake on an aggressive brain malignancy. The finding illustrates that the same sirtuin can exert opposite effects in different cancers, and it suggests SIRT1 activation as a therapeutic direction for glioblastoma.

nodes.label: Glioblastoma growth
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1-mediated deacetylation of p21-activated kinase 1 (PAK1) at lysine 420 hinders autophagy and glioblastoma growth, establishing SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 enzymatic inhibition of PAK1 sits upstream of suppressed glioblastoma progression.
