nodes.label: Ku70-Bax
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 stabilizes the interaction between Ku70 and Bax to enhance the viability of glioma cells, representing an oncogenic function in this cancer type that contrasts with its tumor-suppressive roles elsewhere. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of enhanced glioma cell survival. By keeping Bax sequestered by Ku70, SIRT3 prevents the pro-apoptotic protein from triggering mitochondrial cell death, allowing glioma cells to evade apoptosis. This oncogenic facet complicates the picture of SIRT3 as a universal tumor suppressor and underscores that its net effect depends on cellular context. In gliomas, SIRT3 inhibition might be a strategy to promote tumor cell death.

nodes.label: ERK and STAT3 signaling
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 affects the malignancy of glioma cells mainly by promoting glioma proliferation and invasion through the ERK and STAT3 signaling pathways. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of ERK- and STAT3-driven glioma progression. By sustaining these proliferative and invasive signaling cascades, SIRT7 supports the aggressive growth and spread characteristic of glioma. This identifies SIRT7 as a pro-tumorigenic factor in this brain cancer and suggests that SIRT7 inhibition could suppress glioma progression. The finding adds to the emerging picture of SIRT7 as an oncogenic sirtuin in certain malignancies, where its functions diverge from the longevity-promoting roles of other family members.

nodes.label: p27/CDK2 deacetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 promotes the progression of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia by regulating the phosphorylation and degradation of the cell-cycle inhibitor p27 through deacetylation of cyclin-dependent kinase 2 (CDK2). Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of CDK2-dependent cell-cycle progression in leukemia. By licensing CDK2 activity, SIRT1 promotes the degradation of p27 and thereby removes a brake on cell-cycle entry, fueling leukemic proliferation. This makes SIRT1 a promoter of T-ALL progression and identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential therapeutic strategy to restore p27-mediated cell-cycle control and suppress leukemic growth.

nodes.label: SIRT2 inhibition
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Inhibition of SIRT2 suppresses the in vitro growth and in vivo engraftment of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through diminished deacetylation of LIM domain only 2 (LMO2). Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of LMO2-dependent leukemia suppression. LMO2 is a key oncogenic transcription factor in T-ALL, and its activity depends on deacetylation by SIRT2. Blocking SIRT2 reduces LMO2 function, impairing both the expansion of leukemic cells in culture and their ability to engraft in vivo. This identifies SIRT2 inhibition as a promising approach for T-ALL therapy, targeting a central oncogenic driver in this disease.

nodes.label: LMO2 deacetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Inhibition of SIRT2 suppresses the in vitro growth and in vivo engraftment of T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia cells through diminished deacetylation of LIM domain only 2 (LMO2). Directionally, SIRT2 inhibition sits upstream of LMO2-dependent leukemia suppression. LMO2 is a key oncogenic transcription factor in T-ALL, and its activity depends on deacetylation by SIRT2. Blocking SIRT2 reduces LMO2 function, impairing both the expansion of leukemic cells in culture and their ability to engraft in vivo. nodes.label: Sepsis-induced inflammatory lung injury
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Overall SIRT1 knockout mice are highly susceptible to sepsis-induced inflammatory lung injury due to activation of the proinflammatory transcription factor NF-kappaB. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of heightened inflammatory lung damage. Because SIRT1 normally deacetylates and restrains NF-kappaB, its absence removes a key brake on inflammatory gene expression during sepsis. This unleashes an exaggerated inflammatory response that damages the lung, illustrating SIRT1's protective role in acute inflammatory injury. Restoring SIRT1 activity may therefore help dampen the excessive inflammation that complicates sepsis and contributes to acute respiratory failure.

nodes.label: Hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 promotes the expression of manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD), and this regulation is crucial for the protective effect of SIRT3 on hyperoxia-induced acute lung injury. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of MnSOD-dependent lung protection. By maintaining MnSOD, SIRT3 supports mitochondrial antioxidant defense against the oxidative stress generated by high oxygen exposure. This shields lung tissue from the reactive oxygen species that drive injury during hyperoxia. The finding highlights SIRT3 as a mitochondrial antioxidant guardian in the lung and suggests that strategies to enhance SIRT3 or MnSOD could protect against oxygen-induced lung damage in clinical settings.

nodes.label: ARDS (acute respiratory distress syndrome)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 regulates macrophage polarization to alleviate sepsis-induced acute respiratory distress syndrome via dual mechanisms that are both dependent on and independent of autophagy. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of anti-inflammatory macrophage phenotypes in lung injury. By steering macrophages away from proinflammatory states, SIRT6 dampens the excessive inflammatory response that drives ARDS, while its autophagy-related actions support cellular quality control. This coordinated regulation helps limit lung damage during sepsis.

nodes.label: SNHG10
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The long noncoding RNA SNHG10 upregulates the tumor-suppressive sirtuin SIRT1 in non-small-cell lung cancer by sponging miR-543, relieving microRNA-mediated repression of SIRT1 expression. Directionally, SNHG10 acts upstream of SIRT1 abundance in the NSCLC ceRNA network. By sequestering miR-543, SNHG10 raises SIRT1 levels, and this upregulation underlies the lncRNA's tumor-suppressive activity in lung cancer. The finding highlights how noncoding RNAs can tune sirtuin expression and thereby influence the balance between tumor suppression and tumor promotion in specific cancer contexts.

nodes.label: NSCLC cell proliferation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1, when upregulated by the long noncoding RNA SNHG10, suppresses proliferation of non-small-cell lung cancer cells, acting as a tumor suppressor in this context. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of restrained NSCLC growth. This tumor-suppressive role of SIRT1 in lung cancer contrasts with the oncogenic functions SIRT1 displays in other settings, underscoring the strong context dependence of sirtuin biology. The finding implicates SIRT1 as a mediator of SNHG10's anti-proliferative effects and suggests that sustaining SIRT1 expression may limit NSCLC cell expansion.

nodes.label: circ_0001946
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: The circular RNA circ_0001946 upregulates SIRT1, and the resulting SIRT1 activity promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, circ_0001946 sits upstream of SIRT1 upregulation, which in turn drives oncogenic Wnt signaling. This represents a tumor-promoting axis in lung adenocarcinoma that is opposite to the tumor-suppressive SIRT1 effect mediated by SNHG10 in NSCLC, illustrating how different noncoding RNAs can direct SIRT1 toward opposing outcomes in the same tissue.

nodes.label: Wnt/β-catenin signaling in lung adenocarcinoma
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1, upregulated by circ_0001946, promotes cell growth in lung adenocarcinoma by activating the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of β-catenin-driven proliferation in this lung cancer subtype. This oncogenic SIRT1 function contrasts with the tumor-suppressive anti-proliferative effect SIRT1 exerts in non-small-cell lung cancer when induced by SNHG10, demonstrating that SIRT1's role in lung cancer depends on the tumor subtype and the signaling context.

nodes.label: osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and EMT
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT1 protects non-small-cell lung cancer cells against osteopontin-induced NF-κB p65 acetylation and epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, thereby attenuating osteopontin-driven cell proliferation, migration, and invasion. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of dampened NF-κB signaling and EMT in response to the pro-metastatic cytokine osteopontin. By deacetylating p65 and restraining EMT, SIRT1 limits the invasive and proliferative program that osteopontin triggers in NSCLC cells, supporting a tumor-suppressive role in this context.
nodes.norm_label: osteopontin-induced nf-κb p65 acetylation and emt

nodes.label: phosphoglycerate mutase (K100)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 deacetylates the K100 residue of the glycolytic enzyme phosphoglycerate mutase and facilitates its activation, which results in enhanced NADPH production and accelerated tumor growth in non-small-cell lung cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT2 enzymatic modification of phosphoglycerate mutase sits upstream of increased glycolytic flux and anabolic support for tumor growth. This oncogenic action of SIRT2 in lung cancer contrasts with its tumor-suppressive deacetylation of AKR1C1 in the same disease, illustrating the context dependence of SIRT2's cancer-related functions.

nodes.label: SIRT1 silencing
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Silencing of SIRT1 enhances the cisplatin sensitivity of H1299/cisplatin non-small-cell lung cancer cells by suppressing autophagy. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of reduced autophagic survival signaling and increased susceptibility to cisplatin. Because autophagy can protect cancer cells from chemotherapy-induced damage, its suppression re-sensitizes resistant NSCLC cells to cisplatin. This identifies SIRT1 inhibition as a potential strategy to overcome platinum resistance in lung cancer.

nodes.label: cisplatin sensitivity via autophagy suppression

nodes.label: SIRT2 upregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Upregulation of SIRT2 in non-small-cell lung cancer cells increases their sensitivity to cisplatin treatment, while the opposite modulation reduces responsiveness. Directionally, SIRT2 levels sit upstream of platinum chemosensitivity in NSCLC. Higher SIRT2 expression renders tumor cells more vulnerable to cisplatin-induced killing, suggesting that SIRT2 activity could be exploited to improve the efficacy of platinum-based therapy in lung cancer.

nodes.label: cisplatin sensitivity in NSCLC
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Upregulation of SIRT2 in non-small-cell lung cancer cells increases their sensitivity to cisplatin treatment, while the opposite modulation reduces responsiveness. Higher SIRT2 expression renders tumor cells more vulnerable to cisplatin-induced killing, suggesting that SIRT2 activity could be exploited to improve the efficacy of platinum-based therapy in lung cancer.

nodes.label: cisplatin resistance in lung cancer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 reduces cisplatin resistance in lung cancer by modulating the FoxO3/Cdc10-dependent transcript 1 protein axis. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of restored platinum sensitivity in drug-resistant lung cancer cells. By acting through the FoxO3/CDT1 pathway, SIRT3 counteracts the survival adaptations that underlie cisplatin resistance, making SIRT3 activation a candidate strategy to re-sensitize resistant lung tumors to platinum-based chemotherapy.

nodes.label: Serum SIRT3
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Serum SIRT3 distinguishes lung cancer patients from healthy individuals with an area under the curve of 0.918, an optimal cutoff value of 3.12, a sensitivity of 86.4%, and a specificity of 94%. Directionally, serum SIRT3 levels serve as a diagnostic biomarker for lung cancer. The high accuracy of SIRT3 in discriminating cancer patients supports its use as a blood-based marker for lung cancer screening or early detection, complementing SIRT expression differences observed between tumor and non-tumor lung tissue.

nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

nodes.label: bile acid metabolism orchestration
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 prevents tumor immune evasion and suppresses the development of hepatocellular carcinoma by orchestrating bile acid metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of anti-tumor immunity and restrained HCC growth. By shaping the bile acid milieu, SIRT5 influences the immune microenvironment of the liver tumor, reducing the ability of HCC to evade immune destruction. This tumor-suppressive metabolic function contrasts with SIRT5's glycolysis-reprogramming role that can promote HCC growth, reflecting SIRT5's context-dependent effects in liver cancer.

nodes.label: HCC growth and metastasis via glycolysis reprogramming
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Activation of mitochondrial SIRT5 promotes the growth and metastasis of hepatocellular carcinoma cells via glucose metabolism reprogramming from oxidative phosphorylation to glycolysis. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of the glycolytic switch that fuels liver cancer progression. By favoring glycolysis, SIRT5 supplies the biosynthetic and bioenergetic demands of rapidly growing HCC cells, supporting tumor aggressiveness. This oncogenic role is opposed by SIRT5's bile-acid-metabolism-mediated suppression of HCC, underscoring the dual, context-dependent functions of SIRT5 in liver cancer.
nodes.norm_label: hcc growth and metastasis via glycolysis reprogramming

nodes.label: SIRT1 and SIRT6
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and SIRT6 deacetylate the RNA-binding protein hnRNP A1 to suppress glycolysis and growth in hepatocellular carcinoma. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT6 sit upstream of hnRNP A1 deacetylation, which curtails glycolytic gene expression and tumor growth. By restraining the glycolytic program through hnRNP A1, these nuclear sirtuins act as metabolic tumor suppressors in HCC, opposing the aerobic glycolysis that supports cancer cell proliferation.

nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

nodes.label: stabilized by USP48
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6, stabilized by the deubiquitinase USP48, attenuates glycolysis in hepatocellular carcinoma and impedes metabolic reprogramming, thereby hampering HCC malignancy. Directionally, USP48-dependent stabilization of SIRT6 sits upstream of suppressed glycolytic metabolism and reduced tumor aggressiveness. By maintaining SIRT6 protein levels, USP48 sustains SIRT6-mediated repression of glycolysis, preventing the metabolic shift that fuels liver cancer growth. This identifies the USP48-SIRT6 axis as a potential therapeutic node in HCC.

nodes.label: colorectal cancer via glutamine metabolism and apoptosis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 affects colorectal cancer in a dose-dependent manner by regulating glutamine metabolism and apoptotic pathways. Heterozygous deletion of SIRT1 induces c-Myc expression, enhancing glutamine metabolism, proliferation, autophagy, and cancer formation, whereas homozygous deletion triggers apoptosis, increases cell death, diminishes autophagy, and reduces cancer formation. Directionally, SIRT1 expression level sits upstream of opposing metabolic and survival outcomes in CRC, explaining the dual roles of SIRT1 in colorectal tumorigenesis.
nodes.norm_label: colorectal cancer via glutamine metabolism and apoptosis

nodes.label: SOD2 and PGC-1α regulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT3 improves the resistance of colorectal cancer cells to anticancer drugs through regulation of superoxide dismutase 2 and PGC-1α. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of SOD2- and PGC-1α-dependent protective responses in CRC. By enhancing antioxidant and mitochondrial programs, SIRT3 reduces the vulnerability of CRC cells to chemotherapeutic agents, contributing to drug resistance. This resistance-promoting role should be weighed when considering SIRT3-targeted cancer therapy.

nodes.label: 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 increases the sensitivity of colorectal cancer cells to the chemotherapeutic drug 5-fluorouracil by inhibiting the cell cycle. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cell-cycle arrest, which primes CRC cells for 5-fluorouracil-induced killing. By restraining proliferation, SIRT4 enhances the cytotoxic effect of the drug, suggesting that SIRT4 expression status could predict or improve responses to 5-fluorouracil-based therapy in colorectal cancer.

nodes.label: SIRT1 upregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: FoxQ1-mediated SIRT1 upregulation augments the expression and nuclear translocation of β-catenin and benefits CRC-related intestinal pathological bacteria, thereby enhancing the radioresistance of colorectal cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 upregulation sits upstream of β-catenin-driven survival and radiation resistance in CRC. By promoting β-catenin signaling, SIRT1 helps colorectal cancer cells survive ionizing radiation, which has implications for combining SIRT1 inhibition with radiotherapy to improve treatment outcomes.

nodes.label: CRC radioresistance via β-catenin
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

nodes.label: SIRT1 depletion
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 depletion promotes gastric cancer progression through activation of the STAT3/MMP-13 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of STAT3- and MMP-13-driven tumor progression in gastric cancer. Because SIRT1 normally restrains this pathway, its depletion unleashes STAT3 activation and MMP-13 expression, accelerating GC growth and invasion. This positions SIRT1 as a tumor suppressor in gastric cancer and identifies STAT3/MMP-13 signaling as a downstream mediator of SIRT1's protective effect.

nodes.label: gastric cancer progression via STAT3/MMP-13
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

nodes.label: cisplatin-resistant ovarian cancer cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Overexpression of SIRT2 significantly enhances the sensitivity of cisplatin-resistant counterpart ovarian cancer cells to cisplatin. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of restored platinum sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer cells. By increasing the vulnerability of these cells to cisplatin, SIRT2 may help overcome platinum resistance, a major obstacle in ovarian cancer treatment. This suggests that strategies to augment SIRT2 activity could improve the efficacy of cisplatin-based therapy in resistant disease.

nodes.label: HMGB1 suppression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 expression suppresses the expression and acetylation of high-mobility group box 1 protein, thereby inhibiting migration, invasion, and angiogenesis of ovarian cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of reduced HMGB1-driven metastatic and angiogenic programs. By dampening HMGB1, SIRT1 limits the invasive and blood-supply-supporting behaviors of ovarian cancer cells, supporting a tumor-suppressive role and identifying the SIRT1-HMGB1 axis as a candidate therapeutic target in ovarian cancer.

nodes.label: endometrial cancer growth and cisplatin resistance
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 promotes the growth and cisplatin resistance of endometrial cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of increased tumor-cell survival and reduced sensitivity to cisplatin in endometrial cancer. By supporting proliferative and survival programs, SIRT1 enables endometrial cancer cells to grow and to withstand platinum-based chemotherapy. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential therapeutic target for improving endometrial cancer treatment outcomes.
nodes.norm_label: endometrial cancer growth and cisplatin resistance

nodes.label: endometrial cancer stemness and chemoresistance via MEK/ERK
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 promotes cell stemness and activates the MEK/ERK signaling pathway while repressing chemosensitivity in endometrial cancer. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of stem-like phenotypes and MEK/ERK-dependent survival in endometrial cancer cells. By enhancing stemness and ERK signaling, SIRT2 supports tumor self-renewal and reduces responsiveness to chemotherapy. This makes SIRT2 inhibition a potential strategy to sensitize endometrial cancer to treatment.
nodes.norm_label: endometrial cancer stemness and chemoresistance via mek/erk

nodes.label: SIRT1 inhibition
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 inhibition increases the sensitivity of glioma cells to temozolomide through facilitation of intracellular reactive oxygen species generation. Directionally, SIRT1 inhibition sits upstream of elevated ROS and enhanced drug-induced cell death in glioma. By blocking SIRT1's protective anti-oxidant activity, glioma cells accumulate ROS that sensitize them to temozolomide, the standard chemotherapy for glioblastoma. Combining SIRT1 inhibition with temozolomide may therefore improve treatment efficacy in malignant glioma.

nodes.label: glioma sensitivity to temozolomide via ROS
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md

nodes.norm_label: glioma sensitivity to temozolomide via ros

nodes.label: SIRT3 overexpression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 overexpression in the breast cancer cell line MTR-3 reduces the sensitivity of the resistant cells to tamoxifen. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of diminished responsiveness to endocrine therapy in breast cancer cells. By lowering tamoxifen sensitivity, SIRT3 may contribute to anti-estrogen resistance, complicating endocrine treatment of breast cancer. This is counterbalanced by SIRT4, which enhances tamoxifen sensitivity, highlighting opposing sirtuin functions in endocrine-resistant breast cancer.

nodes.label: tamoxifen sensitivity in MTR-3 breast cancer cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 overexpression in the breast cancer cell line MTR-3 reduces the sensitivity of the resistant cells to tamoxifen. nodes.norm_label: tamoxifen sensitivity in mtr-3 breast cancer cells

nodes.label: breast cancer cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 enhances the tamoxifen sensitivity of breast cancer cells by inhibiting the STAT3 signaling pathway. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of restored endocrine responsiveness in breast cancer. By suppressing STAT3 signaling, SIRT4 makes breast cancer cells more vulnerable to tamoxifen, in contrast to SIRT3 overexpression, which reduces tamoxifen sensitivity. This positions SIRT4 as a potential enhancer of anti-estrogen therapy efficacy in breast cancer.

nodes.label: AMPK activation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: AMPK activation reduces the expression of the oncogenic protein metadherin through enhanced SIRT1 activity, acting independently of GSK-3β in triple-negative breast cancer. Directionally, AMPK activation sits upstream of SIRT1-driven repression of metadherin. Because metadherin promotes cancer progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance, its downregulation via the AMPK-SIRT1 axis represents a tumor-suppressive mechanism in triple-negative breast cancer.

nodes.label: SIRT1 activity in triple-negative breast cancer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: AMPK activation reduces the expression of the oncogenic protein metadherin through enhanced SIRT1 activity, acting independently of GSK-3β in triple-negative breast cancer. Directionally, AMPK activation sits upstream of SIRT1-driven repression of metadherin. Because metadherin promotes cancer progression, metastasis, and chemoresistance, its downregulation via the AMPK-SIRT1 axis represents a tumor-suppressive mechanism in triple-negative breast cancer.
nodes.norm_label: sirt1 activity in triple-negative breast cancer

nodes.label: SIRT7 depletion
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 depletion inhibits tumor growth by activating p38/MAPK signaling in breast cancer. Directionally, SIRT7 loss sits upstream of p38/MAPK pathway activation, which suppresses tumor-cell expansion. Because SIRT7 normally restrains this growth-limiting signaling, its depletion unleashes p38/MAPK activity and curbs tumor growth. This positions SIRT7 as a tumor-promoting factor in breast cancer and identifies the p38/MAPK pathway as a downstream mediator.

nodes.label: p38/MAPK signaling activation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 depletion inhibits tumor growth by activating p38/MAPK signaling in breast cancer. Directionally, SIRT7 loss sits upstream of p38/MAPK pathway activation, which suppresses tumor-cell expansion. Because SIRT7 normally restrains this growth-limiting signaling, its depletion unleashes p38/MAPK activity and curbs tumor growth. This positions SIRT7 as a tumor-promoting factor in breast cancer and identifies the p38/MAPK pathway as a downstream mediator.

nodes.label: SIRT1 knockdown
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Pharmacological targeting or RNAi-mediated knockdown of SIRT1 inhibits cell growth and sensitizes acute myeloid leukemia cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of enhanced drug sensitivity in AML. By restraining SIRT1-driven survival, AML cells become more responsive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors, suggesting that combining SIRT1 inhibition with TKI therapy could improve leukemia treatment outcomes.

nodes.label: tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Pharmacological targeting or RNAi-mediated knockdown of SIRT1 inhibits cell growth and sensitizes acute myeloid leukemia cells to tyrosine kinase inhibitor treatment. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of enhanced drug sensitivity in AML. By restraining SIRT1-driven survival, AML cells become more responsive to tyrosine kinase inhibitors, suggesting that combining SIRT1 inhibition with TKI therapy could improve leukemia treatment outcomes.

nodes.label: shSIRT6-induced DNA repair deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 knockdown-induced DNA repair deficiencies are potently synergistic with NAMPT targeting in acute myeloid leukemia treatment, showing promising in vivo efficacy compared with monotherapy. Directionally, SIRT6 loss-driven DNA repair defects and NAMPT inhibition cooperate to kill AML cells. This dual strategy exploits two vulnerabilities, offering a rationale for combination-based treatments that outperform single-agent therapy in acute myeloid leukemia.

nodes.label: NAMPT targeting in AML
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 knockdown-induced DNA repair deficiencies are potently synergistic with NAMPT targeting in acute myeloid leukemia treatment, showing promising in vivo efficacy compared with monotherapy. This dual strategy exploits two vulnerabilities, offering a rationale for combination-based treatments that outperform single-agent therapy in acute myeloid leukemia.

nodes.label: AIM2 inflammasome-mediated immunity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 enables HPV-infected cervical cancer cells to continue growing by nullifying absent in melanoma 2 inflammasome-mediated immunity. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of suppressed inflammasome signaling and immune clearance in cervical cancer. By inactivating the AIM2 inflammasome, SIRT1 helps HPV-infected cervical cancer cells evade innate immune surveillance, supporting their continued growth. This positions the SIRT1-AIM2 axis as a potential immunotherapeutic target in HPV-driven cervical cancer.

nodes.label: ACC1 upregulation-driven de novo lipogenesis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 contributes to the reprogramming of fatty acid synthesis by upregulating acetyl-coA carboxylase 1 to promote de novo lipogenesis through SIRT3 deacetylation, thereby promoting the invasion and metastasis of cervical cancer cells. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of ACC1-driven de novo lipogenesis and metastatic behavior in cervical cancer. By enhancing lipid synthesis, SIRT3 supports the invasive and metastatic capabilities of cervical cancer cells, identifying SIRT3-ACC1 lipogenesis as a potential therapeutic target.

nodes.label: MHY2245
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: MHY2245, a new SIRT1 inhibitor, exerts antitumor activity against ovarian cancer cells by blocking the pyruvate kinase M2/mTOR pathway. Directionally, MHY2245 sits upstream of suppressed PKM2/mTOR signaling and reduced ovarian cancer cell survival. By inhibiting SIRT1 and consequently the PKM2/mTOR pathway, MHY2245 curbs tumor-cell metabolism and growth. This supports SIRT1 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy in ovarian cancer, where SIRT1 inhibition of HMGB1 also suppresses metastasis and angiogenesis.

nodes.label: pyruvate kinase M2/mTOR pathway
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: MHY2245, a new SIRT1 inhibitor, exerts antitumor activity against ovarian cancer cells by blocking the pyruvate kinase M2/mTOR pathway. Directionally, MHY2245 sits upstream of suppressed PKM2/mTOR signaling and reduced ovarian cancer cell survival. By inhibiting SIRT1 and consequently the PKM2/mTOR pathway, MHY2245 curbs tumor-cell metabolism and growth. This supports SIRT1 inhibition as a therapeutic strategy in ovarian cancer, where SIRT1 inhibition of HMGB1 also suppresses metastasis and angiogenesis.

nodes.label: SIRT5 loss
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 expression is directly correlated with favorable prognosis in pancreatic cancer, as SIRT5 loss promotes glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase 1 acetylation, thus promoting cell proliferation by enhancing glutamine and glutathione metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of GOT1 deacetylation that restrains pancreatic cancer growth. When SIRT5 is lost, GOT1 acetylation rises, boosting glutamine and glutathione metabolism to drive proliferation. This identifies SIRT5 as a tumor suppressor in pancreatic cancer whose levels could inform prognosis.

nodes.label: GOT1 acetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 expression is directly correlated with favorable prognosis in pancreatic cancer, as SIRT5 loss promotes glutamic-oxaloacetic transaminase 1 acetylation, thus promoting cell proliferation by enhancing glutamine and glutathione metabolism. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of GOT1 deacetylation that restrains pancreatic cancer growth. When SIRT5 is lost, GOT1 acetylation rises, boosting glutamine and glutathione metabolism to drive proliferation. This identifies SIRT5 as a tumor suppressor in pancreatic cancer whose levels could inform prognosis.

nodes.label: SIRT6 upregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Upregulation of SIRT6 by the tumor suppressor KLF10 activity influences glycolysis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and distant metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells. Directionally, KLF10-driven SIRT6 upregulation sits upstream of altered metabolic and invasive behaviors in pancreatic cancer. By modulating glycolysis and EMT, SIRT6 shapes the aggressiveness and metastatic capacity of pancreatic cancer cells, indicating that the KLF10-SIRT6 axis may serve as a therapeutic or prognostic target in pancreatic cancer.

nodes.label: as regulated by KLF10
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: Upregulation of SIRT6 by the tumor suppressor KLF10 activity influences glycolysis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal transition, and distant metastasis of pancreatic cancer cells. Directionally, KLF10-driven SIRT6 upregulation sits upstream of altered metabolic and invasive behaviors in pancreatic cancer. By modulating glycolysis and EMT, SIRT6 shapes the aggressiveness and metastatic capacity of pancreatic cancer cells, indicating that the KLF10-SIRT6 axis may serve as a therapeutic or prognostic target in pancreatic cancer.

nodes.label: pancreatic cancer cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 can facilitate chemoresistance of pancreatic cancer cells by regulating their adaptive response to chemotherapy-induced stress. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of stress adaptation and reduced drug sensitivity in pancreatic cancer. By helping tumor cells adapt to chemotherapy-induced stress, SIRT1 enables pancreatic cancer cells to survive cytotoxic treatment. This identifies SIRT1 as a potential target to overcome chemoresistance in pancreatic cancer.

nodes.label: Nrf2/HO-1-mediated ROS suppression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 can promote cisplatin resistance in ovarian cancer by suppressing DNA damage in a ROS-dependent manner via regulation of the Nrf2/Heme Oxygenase-1 pathway. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of reduced ROS, diminished DNA damage, and enhanced survival of ovarian cancer cells treated with cisplatin. By activating Nrf2/HO-1-dependent antioxidant defense, SIRT5 protects ovarian cancer cells from platinum-induced damage, contributing to chemoresistance. This contrasts with SIRT2, whose overexpression enhances cisplatin sensitivity in resistant ovarian cancer cells.

nodes.label: NAM (nicotinamide) and O-acetyl-ADP-ribose
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Sirtuin-catalyzed deacetylation couples the cleavage of NAD+ to the removal of acetyl groups from lysine residues. Each round of deacetylation converts one molecule of NAD+ into nicotinamide (NAM) and O-acetyl-ADP-ribose. NAM then acts as an end-product inhibitor of sirtuins by binding to a conserved pocket adjacent to the NAD+ site, thereby blocking further NAD+ hydrolysis. This product-based feedback links cellular NAD+ status and NAM levels directly to sirtuin enzymatic output.

nodes.label: NAM (nicotinamide)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Nicotinamide is a known potent inhibitor of several classes of ribosylase enzymes that require NAD for their activity, as well as of SIRT1, the class III NAD+-dependent histone deacetylase. NAM acts as an end-product noncompetitive inhibitor of SIRT1 by binding to a conserved pocket adjacent to NAD+, thereby blocking NAD+ hydrolysis. Because NAM is generated by the sirtuin reaction itself, it provides a built-in negative feedback mechanism that can curtail SIRT1 activity when local nicotinamide accumulates.

nodes.label: five classes (I-IV and U)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The sirtuin family has been classified into five distinct classes (I-IV and U) based on a phylogenetic study of sirtuins from a wide range of prokaryotes and eukaryotes. SIR-2.1, Drosophila melanogaster Sir2 (D.mel1), Hst1, and SIRT1 all belong to subclass Ia. Subclass Ib includes Hst2, D.mel2, and various fungi and protozoa sirtuins along with SIRT2 and SIRT3. SIRT4 and SIRT5 belong to classes II and III, respectively. SIRT6 and SIRT7 belong to Class IV, which includes only eukaryotic sirtuins. Sir2 homologues from bacteria with undifferentiated motifs constitute class U.

nodes.label: CobB
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The first bacterial sirtuin was found in Salmonella enterica and was named CobB due to its involvement in cobalamin biosynthesis and propionic catabolism. CobB demonstrates that sirtuins are not restricted to eukaryotes but are also present in prokaryotes, where they regulate various metabolic pathways. In bacteria one or two sirtuins are typically found, and CobB serves as the founding example of prokaryotic sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: Salmonella enterica
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The first bacterial sirtuin was found in Salmonella enterica and was named CobB due to its involvement in cobalamin biosynthesis and propionic catabolism. CobB demonstrates that sirtuins are not restricted to eukaryotes but are also present in prokaryotes, where they regulate various metabolic pathways. In bacteria one or two sirtuins are typically found, and CobB serves as the founding example of prokaryotic sirtuin biology.

nodes.label: homologous recombination
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 activation enhances homologous recombination, a function that could help to decrease tumours by stabilising chromosomes and/or extending the lifespan by maintaining rDNA arrays. In human cells SIRT1 activation enhances homologous recombination. SIRT1 also contributes to telomere maintenance and augments global homologous recombination, linking nuclear sirtuin activity to genome stability and longevity.

nodes.label: XPA deacetylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 controls UV-induced DNA damage repair by deacetylating xeroderma pigmentosum group A (XPA), a protein that is required for the nucleotide excision repair pathway to function properly. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of XPA activity and thereby of nucleotide excision repair. This places SIRT1 in the DNA damage response network and links sirtuin function to the maintenance of genomic integrity following environmental genotoxic stress.

nodes.label: oxidative stress and age-related NAD+ decline
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 has a significant role in oxidative stress response. Increased SIRT1 protein levels counteract oxidative stress and the ageing-related decline in NAD+ levels. In elderly humans SIRT1 protein expression shows a remarkable age-related increase against oxidative stress. Directionally, SIRT1 sits upstream of cellular defence against oxidative damage, and its induction appears to be a compensatory anti-ageing response that mitigates the consequences of declining NAD+ availability.
nodes.norm_label: oxidative stress and age-related nad+ decline

nodes.label: SIRT1 downregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Downregulation of SIRT1 was found to be important in the senescence of different types of endothelial cells. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of cellular senescence in the vascular endothelium. Because SIRT1 normally promotes stress resistance and genomic stability, its decline in endothelial cells is linked to the senescent phenotype. This positions SIRT1 as a potential target for preserving endothelial function and preventing vascular ageing.

nodes.label: endothelial cell senescence
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Downregulation of SIRT1 was found to be important in the senescence of different types of endothelial cells. Directionally, SIRT1 loss sits upstream of cellular senescence in the vascular endothelium. Because SIRT1 normally promotes stress resistance and genomic stability, its decline in endothelial cells is linked to the senescent phenotype. This positions SIRT1 as a potential target for preserving endothelial function and preventing vascular ageing.

nodes.label: induced pluripotency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: By targeting glycolytic enzymes, SIRT2 controls metabolic reprogramming during induced pluripotency. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of the metabolic switch from oxidative to glycolytic metabolism that accompanies reprogramming of somatic cells toward pluripotency. This metabolic control is essential for the establishment and function of primed human pluripotent stem cells, linking sirtuin activity to cell fate determination and stem cell biology.

nodes.label: HIF-1 activity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 regulates HIF-1 activity, which is important for tumour hypoxia responses. HIF-1 protein stability and transcriptional activity are both negatively influenced by SIRT2, with SIRT2-mediated deacetylation necessary for HIF-1α destabilisation and the tumour cell hypoxia response. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of reduced HIF-1α abundance and activity, thereby restraining hypoxia-driven transcriptional programs in tumour cells.

nodes.label: NSCLC cell lines and metastatic melanoma
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The level of SIRT2 is upregulated in non-small cell lung cancer cell lines and in metastatic human melanoma tissues compared to healthy cells and tissues. Directionally, SIRT2 expression is increased in these aggressive cancer contexts. In metastatic melanoma, SIRT2 levels are increased compared to tumours of early stage, suggesting involvement of SIRT2 in the advancement of metastatic disease. SIRT2 therefore represents a potential biomarker and drug target in NSCLC and metastatic melanoma.
nodes.norm_label: nsclc cell lines and metastatic melanoma

nodes.label: acute promyelocytic leukaemia
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 could be a promising drug target for acute promyelocytic leukaemia therapy. Directionally, SIRT2 activity sits upstream of leukaemia cell survival and differentiation programs. Pharmacological modulation of SIRT2 is therefore being explored as a therapeutic strategy in this haematological malignancy, potentially by restoring differentiation or promoting death of leukaemic blasts.

nodes.label: oxidative damage
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT2 has a role in neurodegeneration and protects neural cells from oxidative damage caused by ageing and disease. Directionally, SIRT2 sits upstream of neuronal resilience against oxidative stress. Although SIRT2 is overexpressed in neurodegenerative disorders such as Parkinson's disease, its ability to shield neurons from oxidative injury suggests a protective function in specific contexts, and SIRT2 remains a candidate target for neuroprotective strategies.

nodes.label: N-terminal 101 residues by mitochondrial processing peptidase
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The full-length SIRT3 protein is enzymatically inactive and contains a mitochondrial targeting domain at its N-terminus. Mitochondrial matrix processing peptidase cleaves the N-terminal 101 residues, which then activates the enzyme. Directionally, proteolytic processing sits upstream of SIRT3 catalytic activity within the mitochondrial matrix. This maturation step ensures that SIRT3 functions only after import into mitochondria, where it deacetylates metabolic enzymes.
nodes.norm_label: n-terminal 101 residues by mitochondrial processing peptidase

nodes.label: SIRT3 deacetylase activity
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The deacetylase activity of SIRT3 is required for viral suppression, and during infection SIRT3 keeps membrane potential and mitochondrial pH stable. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of mitochondrial homeostasis during viral infection, supporting antiviral defence. By maintaining mitochondrial function under infection-induced stress, SIRT3 protects cells from viral damage and restricts viral replication.

nodes.label: viral suppression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The deacetylase activity of SIRT3 is required for viral suppression, and during infection SIRT3 keeps membrane potential and mitochondrial pH stable. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of mitochondrial homeostasis during viral infection, supporting antiviral defence. By maintaining mitochondrial function under infection-induced stress, SIRT3 protects cells from viral damage and restricts viral replication.

nodes.label: p53 pathway
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Through the p53 pathway, SIRT3 prevents dysfunction and senescence caused by high glucose levels in endothelial cells by partially abrogating p53 activity. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of dampened p53 signalling and thereby of protection against glucose-induced endothelial senescence. This links mitochondrial sirtuin activity to vascular health and identifies SIRT3 as a potential target for preventing diabetic endothelial dysfunction.

nodes.label: colon cancer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 could also be used as a marker for colon cancer. In colon cancer, SIRT3 deficiency reduces cell proliferation, invasion, and migration while increasing apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT3 expression levels sit upstream of colon cancer behaviour, with loss of SIRT3 restraining tumour aggressiveness. SIRT3 therefore has potential diagnostic and prognostic utility in colorectal cancer.

nodes.label: HIF-1α inhibition and ROS suppression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 stops mitochondrial reactive oxygen species generation, which inhibits HIF-1α and tumour growth. When SIRT3 is overexpressed, it resists the growth of established cancer cell lines. SIRT3 also prevents cancer cell metabolic reprogramming by destabilising HIF1α. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced mitochondrial ROS and HIF-1α stabilisation, thereby opposing the hypoxic and metabolic adaptations that support tumour growth.

nodes.label: SIRT3 activation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 activation prevents amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neurons from developing metabolic abnormalities. ALS motor neurons exhibit hallmark metabolic defects including decreased mitochondrial respiration and increased glycolysis, which arise from systemic NAD+ depletion. SIRT3 activation and/or NAD+ supplementation has been discovered as a treatment for disease phenotypes in both sporadic and familial ALS, restoring normal mitochondrial metabolism and rescuing motor neuron viability.

nodes.label: ALS motor neuron metabolic abnormalities
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT3 activation prevents amyotrophic lateral sclerosis motor neurons from developing metabolic abnormalities. ALS motor neurons exhibit hallmark metabolic defects including decreased mitochondrial respiration and increased glycolysis, which arise from systemic NAD+ depletion. SIRT3 activation and/or NAD+ supplementation has been discovered as a treatment for disease phenotypes in both sporadic and familial ALS, restoring normal mitochondrial metabolism and rescuing motor neuron viability.

nodes.label: mitotic cell division regulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 plays a crucial role in mitotic cell division regulation. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of proper cell cycle progression and mitotic fidelity. In addition to its roles in glutamine metabolism and tumor suppression, SIRT4 contributes to the orderly execution of mitosis, extending the functional repertoire of this mitochondrial sirtuin beyond metabolism.

nodes.label: NSCLC, colorectal cancer, neuroblastoma, and gastric cancer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 is an effective tumour suppressor in non-small cell lung cancer cells, human colorectal cancer, neuroblastoma, and gastric cancer. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of restrained tumour growth across multiple cancer types, in part by inhibiting glutamine metabolism and modulating mitochondrial dynamics. Low SIRT4 expression thereby permits tumorigenic behaviour, and SIRT4 represents a prognostic and therapeutic target in these cancers.
nodes.norm_label: nsclc, colorectal cancer, neuroblastoma, and gastric cancer

nodes.label: hepatocellular carcinoma and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Expression of SIRT4 is considerably downregulated in hepatocellular carcinoma tumour tissues and in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma. Lower expression of SIRT4 promotes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma and hepatocellular carcinoma development. Directionally, loss of SIRT4 sits upstream of tumorigenic progression in these cancers, and its reduced expression is associated with poorer outcomes, supporting SIRT4 as a biomarker and tumor suppressor in HCC and esophageal cancer.
nodes.norm_label: hepatocellular carcinoma and esophageal squamous cell carcinoma

nodes.label: endothelial cells of the umbilical vein and osteoarthritis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: In humans, SIRT4 inhibits inflammation in endothelial cells of the umbilical vein and in osteoarthritis. SIRT4 suppresses the inflammatory response and oxidative stress in osteoarthritis. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of dampened inflammatory signalling in vascular endothelium and joint tissue. By restraining inflammation and oxidative stress, SIRT4 exerts protective effects in osteoarthritis and may help preserve endothelial function.
nodes.norm_label: endothelial cells of the umbilical vein and osteoarthritis

nodes.label: insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: As an outcome of cellular stresses, SIRT4 controls PTEN stability via the insulin-degrading enzyme (IDE). Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of PTEN protein abundance through IDE-mediated degradation. Because PTEN is a key tumour suppressor and negative regulator of PI3K/Akt signalling, SIRT4-dependent control of PTEN stability links mitochondrial sirtuin activity to oncogenic signalling under stress conditions.

nodes.label: AMPK retrograde signaling
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT4 controls ATP homeostasis and uses AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) to mediate retrograde signalling. Directionally, SIRT4 sits upstream of cellular energy sensing and mitochondrial-to-nuclear communication. By modulating ATP levels and engaging AMPK-mediated retrograde signalling, SIRT4 helps the cell adapt its nuclear gene expression to mitochondrial metabolic status under conditions of energy stress.

nodes.label: FOXO3a in lung epithelial cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: In lung epithelial cells, SIRT5-mediated deacetylation of Forkhead protein FOXO3a inhibits apoptosis induced by cigarette smoke extract. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of FOXO3a deacetylation and reduced apoptosis under cigarette smoke stress. By dampening FOXO3a-driven pro-apoptotic signalling, SIRT5 helps lung epithelial cells survive the toxic effects of cigarette smoke, with potential relevance to smoking-related lung pathology.

nodes.label: breast tumor, HCC, and NSCLC cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 is important in the growth of breast tumour cells, hepatocellular carcinoma, and human non-small cell lung cancer tissues. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of tumour growth in these cancer types, and its overexpression indicates a poor prognosis in human non-small cell lung cancer. SIRT5 thereby acts as a tumour-promoting factor in breast cancer, HCC, and lung cancer, making it a candidate therapeutic target.
nodes.norm_label: breast tumor, hcc, and nsclc cells

nodes.label: SHMT2 desuccinylation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT5 is upregulated during cellular transformation and is involved in cancer and its proliferation by desuccinylating serine hydroxymethyltransferase 2 (SHMT2). Directionally, SIRT5 desuccinylation of SHMT2 sits upstream of enhanced one-carbon metabolism and cancer cell proliferation. By activating SHMT2, SIRT5 supports the biosynthetic demands of proliferating cancer cells, contributing to tumorigenesis.

nodes.label: SIRT5 desuccinylation of SDHA
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT5-mediated desuccinylation of succinate dehydrogenase A (SDHA) promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis. Directionally, SIRT5 desuccinylation of SDHA sits upstream of increased growth of clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumours. By activating SDHA and thereby modulating the TCA cycle, SIRT5 supports the metabolic reprogramming that drives this kidney cancer, identifying SIRT5 as a potential target in ccRCC.

nodes.label: clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT5-mediated desuccinylation of succinate dehydrogenase A (SDHA) promotes clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis. Directionally, SIRT5 desuccinylation of SDHA sits upstream of increased growth of clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumours. By activating SDHA and thereby modulating the TCA cycle, SIRT5 supports the metabolic reprogramming that drives this kidney cancer, identifying SIRT5 as a potential target in ccRCC.
nodes.norm_label: clear cell renal cell carcinoma tumorigenesis

nodes.label: H2O2-induced cell death in cardiomyocytes
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: A finding suggests that in cardiomyocytes, SIRT5 is a key moderator in cell death induced by H2O2. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of the cardiomyocyte response to oxidative stress, dampening or modulating hydrogen peroxide-induced cell death. This places SIRT5 in the cardiac stress response network and suggests that modulating SIRT5 activity could influence oxidative injury in the heart.

nodes.label: cellular energy metabolism and AMPK activity under energy stress
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: As a result of energy stress, SIRT5 modulates cellular energy metabolism and AMP-activated protein kinase activity. Directionally, SIRT5 sits upstream of metabolic adaptation and AMPK activation during energy deprivation. By influencing energy metabolism and engaging AMPK signalling, SIRT5 helps cells maintain energy homeostasis under stress conditions, linking mitochondrial deacylation to the cellular energy sensing network.
nodes.norm_label: cellular energy metabolism and ampk activity under energy stress

nodes.label: telomere position effect
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: In humans, SIRT6 is necessary to maintain the telomere position effect. SIRT6 was discovered as the first enzyme that modifies histones to regulate the telomere position effect in human cells, a novel role for SIRT6 in the regulation of age-related genome silencing. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of telomeric chromatin silencing, providing a new approach for telomere chromatin silencing and linking SIRT6 to telomere biology and genome stability.

nodes.label: aging and reprogramming of human iPSCs
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT6 has a part to play in ageing of human induced pluripotent stem cells as well as their reprogramming. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of pluripotent stem cell aging dynamics and the efficiency of somatic cell reprogramming. By influencing these processes, SIRT6 links chromatin-based ageing regulation to stem cell biology and regenerative medicine.
nodes.norm_label: aging and reprogramming of human ipscs

nodes.label: human osteoblasts
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Sirtuin 6 inhibits the generation of reactive oxygen species and glycolysis, which decreases the inflammatory response generated by hypoxia in human osteoblasts. This has therapeutic implications in inflammatory bone resorption. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of reduced ROS and glycolysis and thereby of dampened hypoxic inflammation in bone cells. SIRT6 thus protects osteoblasts from hypoxia-induced inflammatory damage.

nodes.label: SIRT6 downregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Research has shown that senescence of endothelial cells is induced by oxidative stress due to SIRT6 downregulation. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of oxidative stress-driven endothelial senescence. Because SIRT6 normally supports antioxidant defences and DNA repair, its decline leaves endothelial cells vulnerable to oxidative damage and the senescent phenotype, linking SIRT6 to vascular ageing.

nodes.label: endothelial senescence via oxidative stress
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Research has shown that senescence of endothelial cells is induced by oxidative stress due to SIRT6 downregulation. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of oxidative stress-driven endothelial senescence. Because SIRT6 normally supports antioxidant defences and DNA repair, its decline leaves endothelial cells vulnerable to oxidative damage and the senescent phenotype, linking SIRT6 to vascular ageing.

nodes.label: oxidative damage via NRF2 coactivation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: It has been discovered in humans that SIRT6 interacts with the nuclear factor erythroid-derived 2-like 2 (NRF2) for the protection of mesenchymal stem cells from oxidative damage. SIRT6 safeguards human mesenchymal stem cells from oxidative stress by coactivating NRF2. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of NRF2-dependent antioxidant gene expression and thereby of stem cell survival under oxidative conditions.

nodes.label: SIRT6 overexpression
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Compared to healthy cells, SIRT6 overexpression significantly accelerates apoptosis in tumour cells. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of tumour cell death, preferentially killing cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. This tumour-selective pro-apoptotic activity supports SIRT6 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy against cancers that retain SIRT6 expression.

nodes.label: apoptosis in tumor cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Compared to healthy cells, SIRT6 overexpression significantly accelerates apoptosis in tumour cells. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of tumour cell death, preferentially killing cancer cells while sparing healthy cells. This tumour-selective pro-apoptotic activity supports SIRT6 activation as a potential therapeutic strategy against cancers that retain SIRT6 expression.

nodes.label: SIRT6 deficiency
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Lack of SIRT6 decreases the viability of prostate cancer cells while increasing chemotherapeutic sensitivity. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of reduced prostate cancer cell survival and heightened responsiveness to chemotherapy. This indicates that targeting SIRT6 could render prostate cancer cells more vulnerable to cytotoxic agents, supporting SIRT6 inhibition as an adjunct to prostate cancer treatment.

nodes.label: prostate cancer cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Lack of SIRT6 decreases the viability of prostate cancer cells while increasing chemotherapeutic sensitivity. Directionally, SIRT6 loss sits upstream of reduced prostate cancer cell survival and heightened responsiveness to chemotherapy. This indicates that targeting SIRT6 could render prostate cancer cells more vulnerable to cytotoxic agents, supporting SIRT6 inhibition as an adjunct to prostate cancer treatment.

nodes.label: dependent on N- and C-terminal domains
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: The DNA-activated deacetylase activity of SIRT7 is dependent on both the N- and C-terminal domains. The SIRT7 N-terminal domain (NTD) is made up of three helices, and according to the findings SIRT7-NTD has structural similarities to transcription factor regulators and may have a role in DNA binding. Directionally, the SIRT7 NTD sits upstream of DNA binding and enzymatic activation, connecting SIRT7 structure to its chromatin-associated functions.
nodes.norm_label: dependent on n- and c-terminal domains

nodes.label: aging and lifespan of hematopoietic cells
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 has deacetylase activity and plays a critical role in ageing and lifespan of hematopoietic cells in humans. SIRT7 is an influence factor in healthy aging and the development of age-dependent myeloid stem-cell disorders. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of haematopoietic stem cell maintenance and healthy aging, with dysregulation linked to age-dependent blood disorders.
nodes.norm_label: aging and lifespan of hematopoietic cells

nodes.label: glucose availability with mitochondrial biogenesis
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 arginine methylation maintains energy balance by coordinating glucose availability with mitochondria biogenesis. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of the coupling between nutrient (glucose) status and mitochondrial mass. By linking glucose sensing to mitochondrial biogenesis, SIRT7 helps the cell match energy production to substrate availability, contributing to metabolic homeostasis.

nodes.label: rDNA transcription and pre-rRNA cleavage
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Sirtuin 7 is required not only for rDNA transcription but also for particular pre-rRNA cleavage. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of ribosomal RNA synthesis and processing in the nucleolus. By supporting both rDNA transcription and pre-rRNA cleavage, SIRT7 is essential for ribosome biogenesis, connecting SIRT7 to growth, protein synthesis, and cellular proliferation.

nodes.label: DNA repair and chromatin compaction
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 depletion decreases DNA repair and compaction of chromatin, rendering cells more susceptible to genotoxic stressors. SIRT7 is a histone desuccinylase that functionally links to chromatin compaction and genome stability. Directionally, SIRT7 loss sits upstream of reduced genomic stability and increased sensitivity to DNA damage, making SIRT7 important for protecting cells against genotoxic stress.

nodes.label: human stem cell aging as a heterochromatin stabilizer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 antagonizes human stem cell aging as a heterochromatin stabiliser and safeguards chromatin structure. As a heterochromatin stabiliser, SIRT7 counteracts human stem cell ageing. SIRT7 also regulates innate immune modulation and ensures geroprotection during stem cell ageing. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of heterochromatin maintenance and stem cell rejuvenation, protecting stem cells from age-related chromatin deterioration.
nodes.norm_label: human stem cell aging as a heterochromatin stabilizer

nodes.label: SIRT7 inactivation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 inactivation reduces breast cancer metastasis by blocking TGF-β signalling. SIRT7 deacetylase activity inhibits metastasis of breast cancer by antagonising transforming growth factor-β signalling. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of TGF-β-driven metastasis in breast cancer. By promoting TGF-β signalling, SIRT7 supports the metastatic spread of breast cancer cells, and its inactivation curbs this process regardless of changes in original tumour development.

nodes.label: TGF-β signaling
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT7 inactivation reduces breast cancer metastasis by blocking TGF-β signalling. SIRT7 deacetylase activity inhibits metastasis of breast cancer by antagonising transforming growth factor-β signalling. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of TGF-β-driven metastasis in breast cancer. By promoting TGF-β signalling, SIRT7 supports the metastatic spread of breast cancer cells, and its inactivation curbs this process regardless of changes in original tumour development.

nodes.label: colorectal, gastric, and luminal breast cancer
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: In humans, SIRT7 takes part in the genesis of colorectal cancer, gastric cancer, and luminal breast cancer. SIRT7 is overexpressed in multiple cancer tissues, promoting the survival of cancer cells and the maintenance of a transformed state. Directionally, SIRT7 sits upstream of tumorigenesis in these cancer types, and its overexpression supports the transformed phenotype across a broad range of tumours.
nodes.norm_label: colorectal, gastric, and luminal breast cancer

nodes.label: Butein, piceatannol and isoliquiritigenin
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Plant polyphenols notably butein, piceatannol, and isoliquiritigenin (ILQ) have been demonstrated to activate recombinant SIRT1, and are known as sirtuin activating compounds (STACs). Directionally, these natural polyphenols sit upstream of enhanced SIRT1 enzymatic activity. Together with resveratrol, these plant-derived compounds represent natural STACs, and synthetic STACs such as SRT1720 activate SIRT1 substantially more potently.

nodes.label: recombinant SIRT1
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Plant polyphenols notably butein, piceatannol, and isoliquiritigenin (ILQ) have been demonstrated to activate recombinant SIRT1, and are known as sirtuin activating compounds (STACs). Directionally, these natural polyphenols sit upstream of enhanced SIRT1 enzymatic activity. Together with resveratrol, these plant-derived compounds represent natural STACs, and synthetic STACs such as SRT1720 activate SIRT1 substantially more potently.

nodes.label: calorie restriction in lower organisms
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Resveratrol (3, 5, 4'-trihydroxystilbene) is a natural plant polyphenol found in grapes and red wines. In lower organisms, resveratrol replicates the effects of calorie restriction, and mice fed a high-fat diet have lower insulin resistance. STACs interact directly with SIRT1 and other isoforms, and resveratrol remains the most prominent natural sirtuin activator with longevity-relevant effects.

nodes.label: SRT1720
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Many synthetic STACs that are chemically unrelated to resveratrol, such as those with an imidazo[1,2-b]thiazole core including SRT1720, activate SIRT1 substantially more potently than resveratrol. Directionally, SRT1720 sits upstream of enhanced SIRT1 activity, with higher potency than natural activators. These synthetic activators have been used in numerous studies to demonstrate their effect on SIRT1 and are being developed for therapeutic applications.

nodes.label: Sir2 in S. cerevisiae (weakly inhibits human SIRT1)
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Splitomicin inhibits Sir2 in Saccharomyces cerevisiae, but showed weaker inhibition on human SIRT1. Yeast Sir2 and human SIRT2 are inhibited by sirtinol. Directionally, these small-molecule sirtuin inhibitors (STICs) sit upstream of reduced sirtuin catalytic activity, with species- and isoform-selective potencies. Sirtuin inhibitors have also been considered for the treatment of Parkinson's disease, in addition to cancer therapy.
nodes.norm_label: sir2 in s. cerevisiae (weakly inhibits human sirt1)

nodes.label: SIRT1, SIRT2 and SIRT5
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Suramin is a potent inhibitor of many sirtuins like SIRT1, SIRT2 and SIRT5. The majority of known sirtuin inhibitors exclusively inhibit SIRT1 and/or SIRT2, however some also inhibit SIRT3 and SIRT5 with reduced affinity. Cambinol has the most effective efficacy against Burkitt lymphoma cell lines, and Salermide causes apoptosis in cancer cells without relying on p53, with both inhibiting SIRT1 and SIRT2.

nodes.label: Burkitt lymphoma cell lines
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Cambinol has the most effective efficacy against Burkitt lymphoma cell lines. Salermide causes apoptosis in cancer cells without relying on p53. Both Cambinol and Salermide have inhibitory effects on SIRT1 and SIRT2. Directionally, these sirtuin-inhibiting compounds sit upstream of suppressed cancer cell growth, with Cambinol showing particular potency against Burkitt lymphoma among the STIC class of sirtuin inhibitors.

nodes.label: SIRT1 and SIRT2
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: SIRT1 and SIRT2 promote cell proliferation and play a pro-tumorigenic role in lung cancer. Expression of sirtuin 1 and 2 is associated with poor prognosis in non-small cell lung cancer patients. Directionally, SIRT1 and SIRT2 sit upstream of lung cancer cell proliferation and aggressive disease. Their elevated expression is linked to poor prognosis, supporting SIRT1 and SIRT2 as therapeutic targets and prognostic biomarkers in lung cancer.

nodes.label: colon cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: In colon cancer, SIRT3 deficiency reduces cell proliferation, invasion, and migration while increasing apoptosis. Directionally, SIRT3 loss sits upstream of restrained colon cancer aggressiveness and enhanced cell death. SIRT3 could also be used as a marker for colon cancer. These findings indicate that SIRT3 supports the aggressive behaviour of colon cancer cells, and its inhibition may represent an anti-tumour strategy.
nodes.norm_label: colon cancer cell proliferation, invasion, and migration

nodes.label: SIRT3 upregulation
nodes.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins Shedding light on structure, function and regulation of human sirtuins a comprehensive review.md
nodes.description: Upregulation of SIRT3 in breast cancer cells suppresses glycolysis and proliferation, offering a metabolic pathway for tumour suppression. Directionally, SIRT3 sits upstream of reduced glycolytic metabolism and growth in breast cancer cells. By suppressing glycolysis, SIRT3 limits the Warburg-like metabolic program that supports breast cancer proliferation, identifying SIRT3 activation as a potential tumour-suppressive strategy in breast cancer.

nodes.label: glycolysis and proliferation in breast cancer cells
