links.context: Kaempferol is a flavonoid polyphenol reported to possess anti-glycation properties. Along with other flavonoids such as genistein, quercitrin, and quercetin, kaempferol inhibits the glycation process in vitro, and several herbal polyphenols have anti-glycation activities similar to or stronger than aminoguanidine. These compounds act partly through their antioxidant capacity, which reduces the ROS-driven acceleration of protein glycation. Flavonoid-rich herbs and dietary plants are therefore considered promising, relatively safe agents for the prevention of glycation and AGE formation during aging.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
links.context: Quercetin is a flavonoid polyphenol with reported anti-glycation properties. Along with kaempferol, genistein, and quercitrin, quercetin inhibits the glycation process in vitro, and the anti-glycation activities of several polyphenols are similar to or even stronger than the reference inhibitor aminoguanidine. These flavonoids act partly through high antioxidant capacity, which counteracts the ROS that accelerate glycation. Because naturally occurring phytochemicals are relatively safe and available in oral forms, flavonoid-rich herbs are promising agents for the prevention of glycation and AGE formation.

links.source_file: _document_ - COMT How to Optimize Your Supplements for Your COMT Genotype.md
links.context: Quercetin enhances EGCG bioavailability by inhibiting the metabolism and efflux of EGCG, increasing the proportion of the parent catechin available in its bioactive form. As a catechol flavonoid itself, quercetin may also compete for COMT, further slowing EGCG O-methylation and extending its exposure. The quercetin-EGCG combination is therefore studied for synergistic polyphenol effects on metabolism and oxidative stress. This interaction illustrates how co-ingested flavonoids modulate each other's pharmacokinetics.

links.source_file: _document_ - COMT How to Optimize Your Supplements for Your COMT Genotype.md
links.context: Quercetin is a catechol flavonoid, a flavonol whose B-ring bears two adjacent hydroxyl groups, classifying it as a dietary catechol and a COMT substrate. Its catechol structure also enables competitive COMT inhibition at higher doses, influencing both its own pharmacokinetics and those of co-ingested catechols like EGCG. It is among the most abundant flavonoids in the human diet, found in onions, apples, and tea, where it contributes to antioxidant and anti-inflammatory effects. Its metabolism by COMT links dietary intake to genotype-dependent disposition.

Quercetin is a flavonoid classified as a senolytic that inhibits BCL-2 family anti-apoptotic proteins and PI3K/Akt signaling, and is a core component of the D+Q combination with dasatinib. It shows broad senolytic activity and synergizes with dasatinib, and its additional antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties complement its clearance action. The classification is supported by the foundational Zhu et al. (2015) study and subsequent clinical pilots. Quercetin exemplifies a naturally occurring compound with a validated senolytic role.

High-catechol flavonoids such as quercetin, fisetin, and luteolin can inhibit COMT, leading to catecholamine accumulation and worrier-type symptoms during a bulk phase. Slow-COMT individuals are especially advised to avoid these during high catecholamine turnover to prevent adrenochrome pathway fueling.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
links.context: Genistein is an isoflavone flavonoid reported to possess anti-glycation properties. Together with other flavonoids such as kaempferol, quercitrin, and quercetin, genistein inhibits the glycation process in vitro. The anti-glycation activities of these polyphenols are similar to or even stronger than aminoguanidine, and they act in part through trapping reactive carbonyl species and antioxidant capacity. Herbal products and dietary plants containing these flavonoids are therefore considered promising, relatively safe agents for preventing glycation and AGE accumulation during aging.

Genistein is a type of flavonoids, specifically an isoflavone found abundantly in soy, and it shares the redox and signaling properties of the broader flavonoid class. Its structure includes a phenolic A ring that confers antioxidant activity. The directionality is subclass membership within the flavonoid family. A caveat is that genistein also has estrogen-receptor modulatory activity distinct from its antioxidant effects. Genistein's antioxidant actions are complemented by estrogen-receptor signaling, tyrosine-kinase inhibition, and effects on eNOS and NOX, making it a multitarget isoflavone.

Genistein activates NRF2 by covalently modifying KEAP1 cysteine residues, analogous to other electrophilic flavonoids, leading to induction of HO-1, NQO1, and glutathione-pathway enzymes. This reinforces cellular antioxidant capacity. The directionality is thiol modification to NRF2-dependent transcription. A caveat is that genistein's NRF2 activation competes with its other receptor activities, and in vivo magnitude depends on metabolism. Sustained NRF2-driven defenses are thought to contribute to genistein's protection against oxidative DNA damage and metabolic stress.

Genistein inhibits NADPH oxidase, reducing superoxide production in endothelial cells by interfering with NOX assembly and signaling. This contributes to its vasculoprotective profile. The directionality is isoflavone to lowered NOX-derived ROS. A caveat is that genistein's effects on NOX are cell-type specific and can be modulated by its estrogen-receptor activity. By limiting superoxide, genistein also spares nitric oxide from rapid inactivation, improving endothelial function and vascular tone. These effects, combined with suppression of adhesion-molecule expression, underpin its atheroprotective properties in experimental and epidemiological studies.

Genistein enhances nitric oxide bioavailability by upregulating eNOS expression and scavenging superoxide that would otherwise consume NO. The combined effect improves endothelial NO signaling. The directionality is isoflavone to increased bioavailable NO. A caveat is that genistein can also bind estrogen receptors, so part of its vascular benefit may be receptor-mediated rather than purely redox-based. Clinical studies report improved flow-mediated dilation after soy isoflavone intake, consistent with enhanced NO-dependent vasorelaxation in vivo.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
links.context: The inhibition of AGE formation and accumulation in tissues can lead to an increase in lifespan, as concluded from extensive evidence that AGE accumulation accompanies aging and age-related diseases. Because there are no enzymes to remove glycated products, AGEs accumulate as metabolic waste and contribute to tissue senescence. Inhibiting the glycation process and removing existing glycation products may prolong lifespan, and dietary herbal supplements or physiological exercise are advantageous in reducing the AGE burden in the body.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of glycation in the pathogenesis of aging and its prevention through herbal products and physical exercise.md
links.context: A diet restricting advanced glycation end products can effectively reduce the AGE burden in the human body. In renal failure patients, a low-AGE diet produced a 34% reduction in blood CML levels, while an AGE-rich diet increased CML by 29%. Because significant AGE generation occurs when sugars are cooked with proteins, dietary intake is an important exogenous source of glycotoxins. Restricting dietary AGEs is therefore proposed as an effective way to reduce circulating AGE levels and protect against AGE-related organ dysfunction and tissue aging.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is a pyridine nucleotide consisting of a nicotinamide riboside molecule bound to a phosphate group. It is an intermediate of the NAD+ salvage pathway and, when administered orally or intraperitoneally, is rapidly converted into NAD+ in major metabolic tissues such as the liver and skeletal muscle. In healthy subjects, oral NMN at 250 mg/day for 12 weeks elevated NAD+ levels in whole blood, and a 300 mg dose for 60 days raised serum NAD+/NADH levels by about 38%. In mice, oral NMN was absorbed from the intestine within minutes and produced a consistent increase in hepatic NAD+ at 15 to 30 minutes, showing that NMN acts as a direct biosynthetic precursor that replenishes the cellular NAD+ pool.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) promoted telomere lengthening in aged mice, pre-aging mice, and humans. In one study, treating generation-4 mice with NMN in drinking water for 8 weeks lengthened telomeres, dampened the DNA damage response and p53 activation, functionally rescued liver fibrosis, and improved mitochondrial biogenesis and function in a partially SIRT1-dependent manner. The increased NAD+ levels in the liver of NMN-treated mice reversed hyperacetylation of several sirtuin targets, reinforcing sirtuin activity. These effects counteract the telomere shortening and sirtuin repression that accompany DNA damage accumulation, positioning NMN as a nutraceutical candidate to prevent age-related physiological decline.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is an effective intervention against the pathophysiology of type 2 diabetes in both diet-induced and age-induced mouse models. Intraperitoneal administration at 500 mg/kg body weight per day for 11 days substantially ameliorated impaired glucose tolerance and enhanced hepatic insulin sensitivity, with the reversal of gene expression changes related to oxidative stress, inflammatory response, and circadian rhythm partly resulting from SIRT1 activation. NMN also restored glucose-stimulated insulin secretion in aged beta-cell-specific SIRT1-overexpressing (BESTO) mice and aged wild-type mice, and in postmenopausal women with prediabetes, 250 mg/day for 10 weeks increased NAD+ in PBMCs and improved insulin signaling and sensitivity in skeletal muscle.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves insulin sensitivity and signaling, particularly in metabolically compromised settings. In postmenopausal women with overweight or obesity and prediabetes, oral NMN at 250 mg/day for 10 weeks increased NAD+ content in peripheral blood mononuclear cells and improved insulin signaling and sensitivity in skeletal muscle. In mouse models, NMN enhanced hepatic insulin sensitivity and ameliorated impaired glucose tolerance, although these benefits were most pronounced in the most metabolically compromised groups. Notably, NMN had no beneficial effect on glucose metabolism in healthy mice on a chow diet and even impaired glucose tolerance in lean-progenitor offspring, suggesting precursors act best when NAD+ levels are depleted.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) restores insulin secretion that is impaired by inflammation and metabolic stress. In islets cultured with the pro-inflammatory cytokines IL-1beta and TNF-alpha, NMN administration at 100 umol/L restored insulin secretion in a partially SIRT1-dependent manner and corrected inflammation-induced islet dysfunction by reversing changes in genes encoding islet markers essential for glucose sensing and beta-cell differentiation. In mice fed a fructose-rich diet, NMN improved glucose-stimulated insulin secretion, indicating protection against beta-cell failure through an anti-inflammatory mechanism. This action supports NMN's anti-diabetic effects and its capacity to preserve pancreatic beta-cell function under cytokine-driven stress.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves features of Alzheimer's disease by raising NAD+ levels and supporting sirtuin activity. It protects neuronal cells from oxidative stress, prevents beta-amyloid oligomer-induced cognitive impairment and neuronal death, and inhibits JNK activation to reverse Alzheimer's disease pathology in experimental models. NMN is proposed as a nutraceutical to prevent age-related physiological decline and has demonstrated cardio- and vasoprotective actions as well. Alongside nicotinamide riboside, which reduces neuroinflammation, phosphorylated Tau, DNA damage, and hippocampal neuron apoptosis while increasing neurogenesis, NMN represents a dietary NAD+ precursor strategy against neurodegenerative and age-related diseases.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) suppresses inflammation and oxidative stress by downregulating cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2). In LPS-activated mouse and human macrophage cell lines (THP-1 and RAW264.7), treatment with 500 uM NMN decreased pro-inflammatory cytokine production and efficiently alleviated LPS-induced inflammation via the COX-2-PGE2 axis. NMN markedly decreased mRNA expression and extracellular secretion of IL-6 and IL-1beta and lowered cellular prostaglandin E2 levels, while proteins related to the inflammatory response such as RELL1, PTGS2, FGA, FGB, and igkv12-44 were reduced. NMN also suppressed prostanoid biosynthesis and NF-kB signaling, demonstrating broad anti-inflammatory activity in innate immune cells.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) suppresses NF-kB signaling as part of its anti-inflammatory mechanism. In LPS-activated macrophages, proteomics analysis identified that NMN downregulated COX-2 expression and suppressed inflammation-related pathways including prostanoid biosynthesis, LPS/IL-1-mediated inhibition of RXR function, and IL-6 and NF-kB signaling. This downregulation of NF-kB and related pathways decreased extracellular secretion of IL-6 and IL-1beta and lowered prostaglandin E2 levels, alleviating LPS-induced inflammation and oxidative stress. These effects complement the sirtuin-mediated suppression of NF-kB, positioning NMN as a dietary agent that restrains the master pro-inflammatory transcription factor.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) exerts cardio- and vasoprotective actions, protecting against heart failure, ischemia, and reperfusion injury. NMN preserves cardiac mitochondrial homeostasis, prevents heart failure in animal models, and attenuates cardiac fibrosis by regulating oxidative stress and Smad3 acetylation. It also restores angiogenic capacity and attenuates oxidative stress in aged cerebromicrovascular endothelial cells, and rescues endothelial dysfunction and neurovascular coupling in aged mice. By inhibiting inflammation and decreasing oxidative stress, NMN prevents arterial and endothelial dysfunction, supporting its proposed use as a nutraceutical against age-related cardiovascular decline.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) derived from the gut microbiota ameliorates acute pancreatitis injury. In acute pancreatitis mouse models, NMN increased NAD+ levels and activated the SIRT3-PRDX5 pathway, mitigating pancreatic mitochondrial dysfunction, oxidative damage, and inflammation in a partially SIRT3-dependent manner. Acute pancreatitis is exacerbated by gut microbiota dysbiosis, and normobiotic fecal microbiota transplantation induced higher serum NMN levels, enhancing NAD+ biosynthesis in the pancreas. This makes NMN an important mediator of the protective effects of fecal microbiota transplantation and highlights the role of gut microbiota-produced NAD+ precursors in pathological outcomes of the host.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) can selectively stimulate the growth of beneficial gut bacteria such as Bifidobacterium and Lactobacillus. These genera are associated with improved gut health, including prevention of diarrhea, improved gut barrier function, reduced inflammation, and immune system support. NAD+ precursors modulate gut microbiota by providing an energy source for beneficial bacteria, activating sirtuins, and improving gut barrier function. NMN and NR thereby reverse gut dysbiosis and promote beneficial effects at both intestinal and extraintestinal levels, linking dietary NAD+ precursor intake to a healthier gut microbial community.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) reverses gut dysbiosis and protects the intestinal tract. In an experimental mouse model of colitis induced by dextran sodium sulfate, NMN given by gavage at 1 mg/g body weight increased microbial abundance and diversity, improved mucus secretion and tight-junction protein expression, and attenuated intestinal mucosal permeability, protecting against inflammatory bowel disease. Long-term NMN treatment modulated gut microbiota diversity and composition, increasing butyric acid-producing bacteria such as Ruminococcaceae UCG-014 and Prevotellaceae NK3B31 as well as Akkermansia muciniphila, while decreasing harmful bacteria like Bilophila and Oscillibacter. NMN thereby restores intestinal homeostasis and barrier integrity through microbiota remodeling.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) improves intestinal barrier function, which is important for preventing translocation of harmful bacteria and toxins from the gut into the bloodstream. In colitis models, NMN increased the expression of tight-junction proteins and improved mucus secretion, attenuating intestinal mucosal permeability. Long-term NMN treatment also increased the number of goblet cells, mucus thickness, and tight junction protein expression, maintaining the integrity of the intestinal epithelium. NMN and NR share this gut-protective property alongside selective stimulation of beneficial bacteria, and NAD+-precursor-activated sirtuins also protect intestinal endothelial cells against oxidative injury, collectively reinforcing the gut barrier.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is found in a range of foods including edamame beans, avocado, broccoli, cucumber, cabbage, and tomato, according to the first evidence published by Mills et al. (2016). Among the investigated sources, the highest NMN content was found in edamame at 0.47-1.88 mg/100 g and avocado at 0.36-1.60 mg/100 g, with smaller amounts in seafood and raw meats (0.06-0.42 mg/100 g). Milk also contains NMN, with human milk the richest source at 2.1-9.8 uM. These natural occurrences support the idea that a normal diet can contribute to NAD+ precursor intake, though optimal sources remain to be established.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: A sub-chronic 90-day toxicity study in rats established that repeated oral administration of synthetic NMN at doses up to 1500 mg/kg/day appears safe and did not promote toxic effects on body weight, food and water consumption, feed conversion efficiency, or biochemical and blood parameters, although higher doses increased kidney, liver, and adrenal gland weights and elevated hepatic enzymes such as alkaline phosphatase, alanine aminotransferase, and aspartate aminotransferase. Based on these findings, the established upper intake level of NMN for a 60 kg individual was set at 900 mg per day. Human studies at 100-500 mg single doses and 250-300 mg/day over weeks to months reported no adverse effects.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) is unstable in blood, degrading very rapidly even at -80 degrees Celsius. In the first clinical trial of single oral NMN doses (100-500 mg) in healthy subjects, NMN was not detected in plasma, most likely because sample freezing before extraction caused NMN degradation. This rapid degradation complicates accurate measurement of circulating NMN and may explain why plasma NMN levels are kept low and constant, presumably due to balanced NMN distribution from plasma to tissues. In mice, orally administered NMN was quickly absorbed from the intestine, eliminated from circulation within 15 minutes, and rapidly converted into NAD+ in tissues such as the liver and soleus muscle.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: In an oncogenic mouse model, supplementation with NMN (500 mg/kg body weight daily for 13 days) significantly increased the secretory phenotype associated with pro-inflammatory senescence, promoting pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma progression. This raises the hypothesis that dietary supplements that increase NAD+ may be tumorigenic in vivo under stress conditions such as premalignant senescent lesions induced by activated oncogenes. The finding highlights the complex, context-dependent interplay between NAD+ metabolism and cancer biology, cautioning that NAD+ precursor supplementation could accelerate tumorigenesis in certain premalignant settings even as it confers health benefits in normal aging and metabolic disease.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: A case study of 10 critically ill COVID-19 patients over 50 years old reported that an NMN cocktail (83 mL of NMN mixed with 400 mL of water, consumed before breakfast and dinner) was strongly associated with resolution of COVID-19 symptoms. Before treatment, patients had low oxygen saturation, pulmonary infiltrates, and inflammation; post-treatment there was rapid improvement in bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, fever resolution, and lower inflammation biomarkers. One patient who stopped treatment after 3 days experienced relapse with fever and pulmonary infiltrates 8 days later. The rapid clinical improvement suggests NMN may help reverse the potentially fatal cytokine storm triggered by SARS-CoV-2, though larger controlled studies are needed.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) enhances aerobic capacity, as demonstrated in a randomized, double-blind study in amateur runners. NMN also improves mitochondrial function and energy metabolism: long-term administration in drinking water at 100 or 300 mg/kg/day for 12 months increased mitochondrial respiratory ability in skeletal muscle and reversed age-associated gene expression changes in a tissue-specific manner in aged mice. These mitochondrial and aerobic benefits are attributed to NMN raising NAD+ levels, which activates sirtuins and supports oxidative metabolism, energy expenditure, and oxygen consumption, positioning NMN as a performance- and healthspan-enhancing NAD+ precursor.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) rescues endothelial dysfunction associated with aging. In aged mice, intraperitoneal NMN at 500 mg/kg/day for 14 days reversed aging-induced cerebrovascular endothelial dysfunction and rescued neurovascular coupling responses, improving cognitive performance by increasing endothelial NO-mediated vasodilation. NMN also restored angiogenic capacity (capillary-like structure formation, proliferative and migratory capability) and attenuated oxidative stress in aged cerebromicrovascular endothelial cells. These vascular protective effects, which depend on NAD+ restoration and likely SIRT1 activation, prevent arterial and endothelial dysfunction and support NMN's role in preserving cardiovascular and cognitive health during aging.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: CD73 is an ectoenzyme that converts NAD+ and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) extracellularly into nicotinamide riboside (NR), which then requires the NMRK pathway for cellular uptake and conversion back to NAD+. Because the utilization of NR and extracellular NAD+ is limited by the activity of the NMRK pathway, CD73-mediated extracellular processing is an important control point in NAD+ precursor biology. NR itself does not require conversion to enter cells, which partially explains its high availability, whereas NAD+ and its other precursors must be converted to either NR or NAM before entering the cell. A gut transporter for NMN encoded by the Slc12a8 gene has also been identified.

CD73, the rate-limiting ectonucleotidase that converts AMP to immunosuppressive adenosine in the tumor microenvironment, is downregulated following intermittent fasting. Reduced CD73 expression leads to diminished extracellular adenosine, which can relieve adenosine-mediated immune suppression and enhance anti-tumor immunity. The regulation is observed in vitro under fasting-mimetic conditions, linking IF to both metabolic and immunological remodeling. Because adenosine signaling promotes tumor evasion, CD73 downregulation represents a plausible mechanism by which fasting improves cancer therapy outcomes.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: CD157, also called bone marrow stromal cell antigen 1 (BST1), is a glycohydrolase that participates in NAD+ precursor metabolism. It hydrolyzes nicotinamide riboside (NR) into nicotinamide (NAM), which is then further metabolized by gut microbiota into nicotinic acid and routed through the Preiss-Handler pathway to NAD+. In addition, CD157 displays base-exchange activity against both NR and niacin riboside (NAR), interconverting amidated and deamidated precursor pathways. This dual activity means CD157 not only diverts NR toward the deamidated route but also links the two branches of NAD+ biosynthesis, providing alternative substrates that maintain intracellular NAD+ levels depending on tissue and dietary context.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: The gut microbiota can produce nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and this microbe-derived NMN exerts protective effects on host tissues. NMN derived from gut microbiota ameliorated acute pancreatitis by increasing NAD+ levels and activating the SIRT3-PRDX5 pathway in mouse models, and normobiotic fecal microbiota transplantation induced higher NMN levels in serum while enhancing NAD+ biosynthesis in the pancreas. Gut bacteria also produce B vitamins and engage the deamidated NAD+ biosynthesis pathway, and microorganisms in fermented beverages can synthesize NMN and NR. This bidirectional axis positions gut microbes as sources of NAD+ precursors that influence host metabolism and disease outcomes.

links.source_file: _document_ - Pharmacological Effects of Urolithin A and Its Role in Muscle Health and Performance Current Knowledge and Prospects.md
links.context: The production of urolithin A depends largely on the metabolic activities of the gut microbiota. During digestion, polyphenolic compounds such as tannins and anthocyanins undergo enzymatic reactions and metabolic conversions facilitated by microbial enzymes, culminating in the production of urolithin A. This metabolism predominantly takes place in the colon, which houses a variety of microbial groups including Proteobacteria, Clostridium, Bifidobacterium, Eubacterium, and Enterococcus faecium that possess distinct metabolic functions, so individual differences in intestinal microbial composition influence how much urolithin A a person produces and absorbs.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: The NAD+ salvage pathway is the main recycling system for the oxidized coenzyme, and its principal substrates are the amidated precursors nicotinamide (NAM), nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), and nicotinamide riboside (NR). NR taken up directly from the diet enters cells and is phosphorylated to NMN and adenylated back into NAD+, restoring intracellular levels that fall with aging, overnutrition, and disease. The reduced forms dihydronicotinamide riboside (NRH) and dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide (NMNH) have also been shown to promote synthesis. Together with the de novo route from tryptophan and the Preiss-Handler pathway from nicotinic acid, this redundancy lets multiple dietary precursors maintain NAD+ homeostasis across tissues.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases (PARPs) are NAD+-consuming enzymes that transfer ADP-ribose units onto proteins and nucleic acids, playing critical roles in DNA repair and antiviral immunity. During aging, accumulated DNA damage activates PARPs, which depletes NAD+ and reduces SIRT1 activity. In SARS-CoV-2 infection, PARPs inhibit viral transcript translation through ADP-ribosylation, but viral macrodomain proteins hydrolyze these ADPR units, and the compensatory hyperactivation of PARPs consumes NAD+; restoring NAD+ may therefore support the antiviral functions of PARPs. PARPs also consume NAD+ during diabetes-associated DNA repair, contributing to the NAD+/NADH redox imbalance that drives diabetic complications.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: PARPs play a critical antiviral role by inhibiting the translation of viral transcripts through ADP-ribosylation of the viral genome, a process requiring NAD+. However, several viral families including SARS-CoV encode a macrodomain protein that hydrolyses the ADPR units from proteins and nucleic acids, inhibiting this PARP protective effect and facilitating replication and virulence. Excessive PARP activation then occurs to compensate for ADPR hydrolysis, accompanied by NAD+ consumption. This suggests that increasing NAD+ levels may restore the antiviral functions of PARPs to support immunity against SARS-CoV-2, providing a rationale for NAD+ precursor supplementation in COVID-19.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: SARM1 is a NAD+-consuming enzyme, grouped with CD38 and CD157 as an NAD+ glycohydrolase that degrades the coenzyme in signaling and stress pathways. Alongside ADP-ribosyl transferases, poly-ADP polymerases, and sirtuins, SARM1 mediates essential NAD+-dependent processes such as DNA repair, apoptosis, cell survival, lifespan regulation, and metabolic adjustments. Its NAD+ consumption contributes to the constant synthesis-catabolism-recycling cycle that sustains NAD+ levels, and disturbances that shift this balance, such as aging or infection, can reduce NAD+ availability. Dietary precursors like NMN and NR counter this by replenishing the NAD+ pool consumed by these signaling enzymes.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: SARM1 (sterile alpha and Toll/interleukin-1 receptor motif-containing 1) is an additional NAD+-depleting enzyme that uses NAD+ to promote axonal degeneration after injury, thereby decreasing overall NAD+ content. Axonal degeneration is an early event in acute cerebral injury and in chronic neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases, and it is caused by excitotoxicity, during which neurons undergo strong NAD+ depletion. Preserving axonal NAD+ to supply damage-induced SARM1 activation has been proposed as one of two mechanisms underlying the neuroprotective effects of nicotinamide riboside, which can protect neurons from excitotoxicity-induced axonal degeneration.

links.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
links.context: SARM1 is an NAD+-consuming enzyme that, along with PARP1, PARP2, and CD38, can deplete cellular NAD+ pools and compromise sirtuin function. Directionally, SARM1 activity sits upstream of NAD+ depletion and impaired sirtuin signaling. Its activity is particularly relevant in neuronal contexts, where NAD+ depletion drives axonal degeneration. By consuming NAD+ upon injury or stress, SARM1 can starve sirtuins of their co-substrate at the very moment when their protective functions are most needed. This makes SARM1 an attractive therapeutic target for neurodegenerative conditions, where preventing NAD+ loss could preserve both axonal integrity and sirtuin activity.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: NAMPT (nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase) is the rate-limiting enzyme that converts nicotinamide into nicotinamide mononucleotide in the NAD+ salvage pathway. A significant cause of age-associated NAD+ decline is the decrease in NAMPT-mediated biosynthesis: NAMPT protein and NAD+ levels fall in white adipose tissue and skeletal muscle of old mice, reducing the activity of NAD+-dependent enzymes such as sirtuins. Inhibiting NAMPT decreases cell growth and increases susceptibility to oxidative stress, a concept being explored for cancer therapy, whereas NMN and NR bypass NAMPT to reverse the cell death it induces, underscoring NAMPT as the central control point of endogenous NAD+ production.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: NAMPT (nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase) is the rate-limiting enzyme that converts nicotinamide (NAM), the most common NAD+ precursor in mammals, into nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN). This step requires more than three ATP equivalents, making it energetically more costly than the NMRK-mediated conversion of nicotinamide riboside (NR) to NMN, which needs only a single ATP. NAMPT expression and NAD+ content decline in multiple tissues with aging and overnutrition, and decreased NAMPT is a major cause of age-related NAD+ decline. NMN subsequently serves as the direct substrate for NMNAT, which generates the essential coenzyme NAD+.

links.source_file: _document_ - sirtuins in health and disease s41392-022-01257-8.md
links.context: NAMPT condenses nicotinamide with 5-phosphoribosyl-1-pyrophosphate (PRPP) to form NMN, the rate-limiting step of the NAD+ salvage pathway. Directionally, NAMPT sits upstream of NMN and NAD+ biosynthesis. This recovers nicotinamide that would otherwise feedback-inhibit sirtuins, and AMPK and SIRT1 both induce NAMPT, creating a positive loop for NAD+ and sirtuin activity. Because NAMPT is rate-limiting, its regulation largely determines NAD+ availability in most tissues. Preserving or inducing NAMPT is thus a central strategy for maintaining sirtuin function and NAD+-dependent metabolism.

links.source_file: _document_ - The Sirtuin Network Linking NAD+ Metabolism, Mitochondrial Function, and Metabolic Homoeostasis.md
links.context: NAMPT (nicotinamide phosphoribosyltransferase) is the rate-limiting enzyme of the NAD+ salvage pathway, converting nicotinamide into nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) in an energetically costly step. NAMPT activity therefore determines how much NAD+ precursor is available to fuel sirtuins and other NAD+-consuming enzymes such as CD38 and the poly(ADP-ribose) polymerases. Directionally, NAMPT sits upstream of NAD+ pool size and sirtuin activity. Because NAMPT couples cellular energy state to NAD+ biosynthesis, it is a primary node linking metabolism to sirtuin function and a key target for interventions aimed at restoring NAD+ during aging.

Neuroinflammation and Microgliosis are reciprocally linked entities in the neuromelanin knowledge graph, reflecting their frequent co-occurrence and shared relevance to catecholamine biology or Parkinson's disease. Directionally, the graph relation is symmetric, although biologically Neuroinflammation and Microgliosis may occupy distinct mechanistic roles. Their association is significant because both contribute to the chemical and pathological network that defines vulnerability of pigmented neurons. A caveat is that a bidirectional link denotes an association rather than a proven direct causal mechanism between the two entities.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is widely considered a hepatic manifestation of metabolic syndrome as it is found to be associated with type 2 diabetes, obesity, and insulin resistance, and sirtuins are downregulated in NAFLD patients, a state characterized by liver steatosis. Raising NAD+ through nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation can restore sirtuin-driven fatty acid oxidation, inhibit lipogenesis, and reduce cholesterol levels, thereby improving liver health and reducing fat accumulation through induction of the mitochondrial unfolded protein response.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: SOD2 (manganese superoxide dismutase) is the mitochondrial antioxidant enzyme that eliminates superoxide generated during respiration. Its activity is regulated by acetylation, with SIRT3-mediated deacetylation increasing SOD2 activity. When NR raises NAD+ and activates SIRT3, SOD2 acetylation decreases, mitochondrial SOD2 activity rises, and mitochondrial reactive oxygen species levels fall. This reduced mitochondrial ROS burden lessens oxidative damage and supports mitochondrial quality control, contributing to NR's protective effects against oxidative stress, inflammasome activation, and age-related mitochondrial dysfunction in tissues such as the myocardium, skeletal muscle, and neurons.

IL-1a is an apical SASP amplifier that sits at the top of the inflammatory cascade, and its cleavage by caspase-5 or calpain is essential for full SASP regulatory function. Cell-surface and secreted IL-1a engage IL-1R, activating MyD88-NF-kB signaling that sustains the SASP and induces paracrine senescence, and it also induces downstream factors such as CCL20 and Activin A. It is thus a master initiator rather than merely a component of the secretome. Its centrality makes IL-1a a key mechanistic and therapeutic node in senescence-associated inflammation.

IL-1a is a primary SASP factor that induces paracrine senescence in neighboring cells by engaging IL-1R and activating MyD88-NF-kB signaling, which drives growth arrest in recipients. As an apical amplifier, it both sustains the SASP in the sender and converts neighbors into senescent cells, and its cleavage is required for full activity. This makes IL-1a a key transmissible effector of senescence spread, with MyD88 and IRAK1 as required downstream nodes. IL-1R blockade can therefore restrain the paracrine propagation of senescence.

SIRT1 directly regulates BDNF transcription by deacetylating and repressing Hes1, a transcriptional repressor of BDNF, thereby relieving inhibition and promoting neuronal survival. Directionally, SIRT1 deacetylates Hes1, which induces BDNF. This links sirtuin activity to neurotrophic support, and it is a mechanism for SIRT1's neuroprotective and cognitive benefits. By removing the Hes1 brake on the BDNF promoter, SIRT1 increases BDNF expression in the brain. This regulation is engaged by caloric restriction and exercise, both of which elevate BDNF through SIRT1-dependent pathways.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Butyrate, a short-chain fatty acid produced by gut bacteria such as Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Eubacterium rectale, and Roseburia, reduces adiposity by inhibiting intestinal cholesterol biosynthesis and promoting beneficial metabolic effects including insulin secretion, insulin sensitivity, and energy expenditure. Butyrate can also increase satiety and gut motility by upregulating the expression of peptide YY and glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1). In studies where NR supplementation enriched butyrate-producing Firmicutes, these metabolic benefits contributed to protection against high-fat diet-induced weight gain, and fecal transfer reproduced the effect, underscoring butyrate as a key mediator of microbiota-driven metabolic health.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Yeast-mediated production of nicotinamide riboside (NR) and nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN) was demonstrated in craft beers, with hop indicating a role in enhancing NR levels during fermentation. This finding opens new perspectives for enriched sources of NAD+ precursors through fermented foods and beverages. Additionally, fructophilic lactic acid bacteria have been investigated for biotechnological production of NMN and NR for functional probiotic products and supplements. These microbial routes complement natural dietary sources such as vegetables, meat, milk, and mushrooms, and could enable the development of new functional foods and biotechnological strategies to maintain and enhance the physiological benefits of NAD+ precursors.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Although nicotinamide (NAM) effectively increases NAD+ in tissues, it also exerts an inhibitory effect on sirtuins and PARP activity, a property that distinguishes it from the other precursors NMN and NR. At high doses, NAM is methylated by nicotinamide N-methyltransferase to generate N1-methylnicotinamide for elimination in urine, which can lower the cellular methyl pool over time. This depletion could reduce DNA and protein methylation and alter gene expression patterns and protein activity, since DNA methylation in gene promoter regions is typically associated with transcriptional repression. These effects may explain why NR administration raises NAD+ levels more than NAM treatment in some studies.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Nicotinamide (NAM), the amide form of vitamin B3 and a product released from NAD+-consuming reactions, inhibits PARP activity while being effective at increasing NAD+ levels in tissues. At high doses, NAM is metabolized by nicotinamide N-methyltransferase into N1-methylnicotinamide for urinary elimination, which can progressively lower the cellular methyl pool, potentially reducing DNA and protein methylation and altering gene expression and protein activity. This dual role as both NAD+ precursor and PARP/sirtuin inhibitor distinguishes NAM from NMN and NR, which elevate NAD+ without this inhibitory action, and may explain differences in their metabolic outcomes.

Nicotinamide binds the C-pocket of SIRT1 at high concentrations, blocking NAD+ re-entry and acting as a feedback inhibitor that links SIRT1 activity to cellular NAD+ salvage status. Directionally, nicotinamide sits upstream of SIRT1 inhibition. This natural brake is relieved when the NAD+/nicotinamide ratio is high, for example during caloric restriction, and it rationalizes NAD+ precursor supplementation to disinhibit sirtuins. By binding the C-pocket, nicotinamide competes with the catalytic cycle and reduces SIRT1 output. This feedback regulation distinguishes sirtuins from many other enzymes and is central to NAD+ biology.

links.source_file: _document_ - Rejuvenating Sirtuins The Rise of a New Family of Cancer Drug Targets.md
links.context: Nicotinamide, a product of the sirtuin deacetylation reaction itself, is a micromolar non-competitive inhibitor of SIRT1 and SIRT2 that interacts with the C (nicotinamide) pocket of the catalytic site. It was one of the first endogenous compounds studied as a sirtuin inhibitor and inspired the search for NAD+ and nicotinamide analogs. SIRT1 inhibition with nicotinamide was reported to have anticancer activity in B-cell chronic lymphocytic leukemia and prostate cancer. Its limitations, and those of NAD+ analogs, lie in modest potency and limited therapeutic potential, which motivated development of more potent scaffolds.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: NRH (dihydronicotinamide riboside) is the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside and has recently been shown to promote NAD+ synthesis. Alongside NMNH (dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide), the reduced form of nicotinamide mononucleotide, NRH expands the repertoire of NAD+ precursors beyond the amidated molecules nicotinamide, NMN, and NR. These reduced precursors are additional substrates for the salvage pathway and are considered orally bioavailable NAD+ precursors. Their discovery illustrates the redundancy of NAD+ biosynthetic routes and suggests that multiple dietary and pharmacological compounds can contribute to maintaining intracellular NAD+ levels across tissues.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: NRH, the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside, is bioavailable in mice and increases NAD+ in both cultured cells (5-10-fold above the baseline) and in mice, in a more potent and faster manner than NR, and it is detectable in circulation after oral intake or intraperitoneal injection. A NMRK-independent pathway for the NRH-induced NAD+ increase has been demonstrated, consistent with the recent discovery of a novel biosynthetic route of NAD+ from NRH through the NMNH intermediate, where adenosine kinase (ADK) acts as an NRH kinase. The presence of endogenous NRH in the liver of mouse models was confirmed, establishing NRH as a valid natural precursor of NAD+.

links.source_file: _document_ - Nicotinamide Riboside—The Current State of Research and Therapeutic Uses.md
links.context: Since nicotinamide riboside (NR) is unstable in blood circulation, partially due to degradation to nicotinamide, its ability to reach peripheral tissues after oral administration is compromised, and this limitation could be overcome by the administration of NRH, the reduced form of NR, which appears to be more stable than NR and does not undergo direct degradation in plasma. NRH is detectable in circulation after oral intake or intraperitoneal injection, and it increases NAD+ in both cultured cells (5-10-fold above the baseline) and mice, in a more potent and faster manner than NR, through a NMRK-independent pathway in which adenosine kinase acts as an NRH kinase.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: NMNH (dihydronicotinamide mononucleotide) is the reduced form of nicotinamide mononucleotide and has been shown to promote NAD+ synthesis. Together with NRH, the reduced form of nicotinamide riboside, NMNH adds to the set of NAD+ precursors available for cellular salvage and NAD+ replenishment. These reduced precursors demonstrate that the NAD+ metabolic cycle is more flexible than initially recognized, providing alternative routes to boost NAD+ levels beyond the classic precursors tryptophan, nicotinamide, nicotinic acid, NMN, and NR, and supporting efforts to develop effective strategies for preventing NAD+ decline in aging and disease.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: SLC12A8 is a transporter encoded by the gene SLC12A8 that has been proposed to mediate cellular uptake of nicotinamide mononucleotide (NMN), in addition to the CD73-mediated dephosphorylation route in which NMN is converted extracellularly to nicotinamide riboside for uptake. The expression of a gut transporter reinforces that NMN could be made bioavailable through oral delivery, and the presence of such a transporter in the intestine supports the idea that dietary NMN can enter the circulation. These uptake mechanisms complement each other and explain how orally administered NMN is rapidly absorbed from the intestine into the bloodstream and converted to NAD+ in tissues.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: NAAD (nicotinic acid adenine dinucleotide) is a product of NR utilization in humans and a biomarker of increased NAD+ metabolism. NR supplementation raised NAAD by 4.5-fold in blood, and healthy middle-aged adults taking 1 g/day NR for 6 weeks showed around a fivefold increase in blood NAAD. In another study, NAAD was undetectable before NR supplementation but increased by approximately 2,900% after single doses of up to 1 g NR. These findings corroborate studies in mice showing that the deamidated Preiss-Handler pathway predominates after NR intake, making NAAD a sensitive readout of the deamidated route of NAD+ precursor metabolism.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: Combined metabolic activators (CMAs), consisting of NR (1 g), l-carnitine tartrate (3.73 g), N-acetylcysteine (2.55 g), and serine (12.35 g), improved COVID-19 outcomes in clinical trials. Patients taking the mixture orally for 14 days had significantly faster complete recovery times than placebo (6.6 vs 9.3 days in a phase 2 study and 5.7 vs 9.2 days in a phase 3 study). CMAs were found to reinforce the immune response and regulate amino acid and lipid metabolism, and patients showed improvements in plasma levels of inflammation and antioxidant metabolism-related biomarkers including alanine aminotransferase, lactate dehydrogenase, creatinine, glucose, and proteins. NR within the mixture contributes NAD+ restoration supporting antiviral PARP function.

links.source_file: _document_ - NAD+ Precursors Nicotinamide Mononucleotide (NMN) and Nicotinamide Riboside (NR) Potential Dietary Contribution to Health.md
links.context: The SARS-CoV-2 macrodomain is a viral protein that hydrolyses the ADP-ribose (ADPR) units added by PARPs to proteins and nucleic acids, thereby inhibiting the protective antiviral effect of PARPs and facilitating viral replication and virulence. Because PARPs require NAD+ to ADP-ribosylate viral transcripts, this counteraction leads to excessive PARP activation and NAD+ consumption during infection, dysregulating the NAD+ metabolome. Restoring NAD+ levels with precursors may therefore restore PARP antiviral function and support innate immunity to SARS-CoV-2, connecting NAD+ metabolism directly to COVID-19 severity and immune defense.

links.source_file: _document_ - Sirtuins and their Biological Relevance in Aging and Age-Related Diseases.md
links.context: SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 on NF-κB (p65) target-gene promoters to repress NF-κB-dependent inflammation, and conversely NF-κB activation opposes SIRT6's anti-inflammatory/genome-stability program in aging; Table 3 lists NF-κB among negative regulators of SIRT6 (Kawahara et al., 2009, Cell).

SIRT6 inhibits isoproterenol-induced cardiac hypertrophy through multiple parallel pathways: promoting autophagy via FoxO3 nuclear retention from Akt attenuation, decreasing p300 and NF-kB p65 acetylation, blocking IGF-Akt signaling through c-Jun, and suppressing STAT3. Each of these inputs converges on dampening the pathological growth response, making SIRT6 a consistently protective factor in cardiac hypertrophy.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of the dynamic epigenetic landscape in senescence_orchestrating SASP expression.md
links.context: SIRT6 represses LINE-1 retrotransposons by maintaining repressive chromatin at L1 loci through its deacetylase and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activities. SIRT6 recruits KAP1 and HP1 to deposit and maintain heterochromatin marks that silence LINE-1 elements, and this silencing declines with age as SIRT6 levels fall. Loss of SIRT6 permits LINE-1 derepression, and activating SIRT6 is explored as a strategy to suppress retrotransposon-driven inflammation in aging. Restoring SIRT6 activity may therefore help suppress retrotransposon-driven inflammation in aging.

links.source_file: _document_ - The role of the dynamic epigenetic landscape in senescence_orchestrating SASP expression.md
links.context: In response to DNA damage signaling, SIRT6 moves away from gene promoters and repetitive loci to sites of DNA breaks, where it recruits DNA repair factors and modifies local chromatin. At damage sites, SIRT6 promotes the deacetylation of H3K56 and other substrates, facilitating efficient double-strand break repair. This mobilization from LINE-1 loci to damage sites simultaneously couples the DNA damage response to derepression of retrotransposons during aging, linking genomic stress to innate immune activation.

SIRT6 is a nuclear sirtuin enriched at heterochromatic and telomeric regions, where it deacetylates H3K9 and H3K56 and performs mono-ADP-ribosylation of KAP1. Its heterochromatin association is critical for genome stability, telomere maintenance, and suppression of repetitive elements such as LINE-1. SIRT6 thus integrates chromatin regulation with metabolic control of glycolysis, DNA repair, and inflammation. Loss of SIRT6 produces a pronounced premature-aging phenotype, highlighting its non-redundant role in the nucleus.

SIRT6 possesses both deacetylase and mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activities, the latter being particularly important for its chromatin functions. Through ADP-ribosylation of KAP1, SIRT6 recruits HP1α to LINE-1 loci, promoting heterochromatinization and silencing of retrotransposons. The directionality is that SIRT6 is the enzyme and KAP1 (and downstream HP1α) the recipients of the ADP-ribose modification. This activity is independent of its deacetylase function and is selectively enhanced by certain natural activators such as fucoidan.

SIRT6 is required for efficient base-excision repair (BER), the pathway that removes oxidized and alkylated bases, and SIRT6-deficient cells accumulate DNA damage from defective BER. SIRT6 supports BER in part by mono-ADP-ribosylating and recruiting repair factors such as PARP1 and by maintaining heterochromatin at damaged sites. Directionally, SIRT6 activity sits upstream of proper BER execution. This function explains the genomic instability and premature aging of SIRT6 knockout mice, and links SIRT6 to tumor suppression, since loss of SIRT6-dependent repair predisposes cells to mutation accumulation and oncogenic transformation.

SIRT6 is the clearest anti-Warburg sirtuin: it corepresses HIF-1alpha and suppresses transcription of glycolytic enzymes (glucose transporters, Hexokinase 2) and deacetylates histone H3 at ERK1/2 promoters. Loss of SIRT6 permits Warburg-like aerobic glycolysis; its restoration suppresses glycolysis in HCC/glioma and enhances radiosensitivity in lung cancer.

Activated SIRT6 rapidly deacetylates histone H3K9ac and H3K56ac at chromatin, promoting compaction and facilitating DNA-repair and silencing programs. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically removes these active marks. Loss of H3K56ac in particular is associated with genome stability and stress resistance, and H3K9ac removal at specific promoters silences glycolytic, inflammatory, and other target genes. This chromatin action underlies SIRT6's roles in longevity and tumor suppression, and it is complemented by SIRT6's mono-ADP-ribosyltransferase activity, which recruits repressive complexes to repetitive elements and DNA-damage sites.

By suppressing glycolysis and pushing tumor cells toward oxidative metabolism or autophagy, SIRT6 activators such as UBCS039 display tumor-suppressive activity. Directionally, SIRT6 activation sits upstream of reduced Warburg glycolysis. This restrains the aerobic-glycolytic phenotype that fuels cancer growth, complementing SIRT6's repression of HIF-1α and c-MYC and its deacetylation of H3K9 at glycolytic promoters. It is a mechanistic rationale for SIRT6 activation in oncology, and SIRT6 deletion in a large fraction of cancer cell lines indicates that restoring SIRT6-dependent metabolic control could constrain tumor metabolism.

SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at the promoters of NF-κB target genes, reducing their transcription and thereby dampening inflammation. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically represses NF-κB-driven loci through chromatin modification. This complements SIRT6's direct promotion of p65 proteasomal degradation and underscores its anti-inflammatory role. Loss of SIRT6 elevates H3K9ac and inflammatory output, contributing to the pro-inflammatory phenotype of SIRT6-deficient tissues. Together with SIRT1, SIRT6 thus provides both chromatin-level and protein-level restraint on the NF-κB pathway that drives chronic inflammation in aging and disease.

SIRT6 overexpression suppresses NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses, as shown in models such as osteoarthritis development where cytokine production is reduced. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of inhibited NF-κB inflammation. This protection arises from both chromatin deacetylation of NF-κB target genes and promotion of p65 degradation, providing redundant brakes on the pathway. It positions SIRT6 as a nuclear inflammation brake, and its loss derepresses inflammatory gene programs. This anti-inflammatory function is part of SIRT6's broader protective phenotype, alongside its roles in DNA repair, metabolism, and the suppression of age-related pathologies.

SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 in pancreatic β-cells, increasing expression of the glucose transporter GLUT2 and maintaining glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically activates FoxO1 in β-cells. This preserves β-cell identity and insulin-secretory competence under metabolic stress, and SIRT6-deficient β-cells lose GLUT2 and glucose responsiveness. It reveals a β-cell-specific metabolic role for SIRT6, distinct from its nuclear chromatin functions, and is consistent with SIRT6's broader maintenance of glucose homeostasis through suppression of TXNIP and restraint of insulin/IGF signaling.

SIRT6 promotes AMPK expression, which upregulates the antioxidant genes manganese superoxide dismutase (MnSOD) and catalase, suppressing oxidative stress. Directionally, SIRT6 induces AMPK, which upregulates MnSOD. Higher MnSOD lowers mitochondrial superoxide, and the combination of MnSOD and catalase upregulation provides coordinated ROS detoxification. This antioxidant program underlies many of SIRT6's protective phenotypes, including genomic stability, metabolic health, and delayed aging. It complements SIRT6's direct chromatin functions and shows that SIRT6 engages the energy-sensing AMPK axis to reinforce cellular antioxidant defense.

Through AMPK, SIRT6 upregulates catalase expression, enhancing detoxification of mitochondrial and cytosolic hydrogen peroxide. Directionally, SIRT6 induces AMPK, which upregulates catalase. Combined with MnSOD upregulation, this strengthens cellular antioxidant capacity and limits oxidative damage to proteins, lipids, and DNA. It contributes to SIRT6's role in genomic stability and healthy aging, and it complements SIRT6's direct regulation of antioxidant and stress-response transcription factors. The AMPK-dependent antioxidant program is one of several mechanisms by which SIRT6 protects cells from the oxidative stress that accumulates with age.

Overexpression of SIRT6 in the brain via in vivo gene transfer enhances Nrf2 signaling and reduces oxidative stress, linking SIRT6 to antioxidant transcription. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of Nrf2 pathway activation. This complements SIRT6's AMPK/MnSOD/catalase axis, providing multiple redundant antioxidant mechanisms. It reinforces SIRT6's role in neuronal and systemic antioxidant defense, and suggests that SIRT6 activation could protect the aging brain from oxidative injury. The convergence of SIRT1 and SIRT6 on Nrf2 highlights the importance of this transcription factor in sirtuin-mediated cytoprotection.

SIRT6 inhibits the Janus kinase 2/STAT3 pathway, suppressing growth and survival signaling in gastric cancer. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of JAK2/STAT3 blockade. This restrains STAT3-driven proliferation and is part of SIRT6's tumor-suppressive repertoire, with SIRT6 loss associated with increased STAT3 activity and tumor aggressiveness. It adds a cytokine-receptor-linked mechanism to SIRT6's anti-cancer actions, complementing its repression of HIF-1α, c-MYC, and glycolysis. Because STAT3 integrates multiple growth and inflammatory signals, its suppression by SIRT6 is relevant to both oncology and chronic inflammation.

SIRT6 blocks IGF-Akt signaling and thereby cardiac hypertrophy development by targeting c-Jun, interrupting a pro-hypertrophic survival pathway. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of IGF-Akt repression. This protects the heart from maladaptive growth, and SIRT6 knockout mice develop cardiac hypertrophy that is abrogated when IGF signaling is inhibited in vivo. It complements SIRT6's anti-fibrotic actions in cardiovascular tissue and illustrates the importance of restraining growth-factor signaling in the heart. SIRT6's co-repression of c-Jun-dependent transcription at the chromatin level links epigenetic control to cardiac remodeling.

SIRT6 inactivates TGF-beta1/Smad2 signaling to prevent myofibroblast differentiation, inhibits TGF-beta-induced cellular senescence, and blocks EMT during IPF through TGF-beta1/Smad3. SIRT6 is thus a master suppressor of the fibrotic cascade in lung fibrosis, whereas SIRT7 decline has a profibrotic effect via Smad3 changes.

SIRT6 suppresses osteogenic transdifferentiation of vascular smooth-muscle cells via repression of runt-related transcription factor 2 (Runx2), limiting vascular calcification. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of inhibited VSMC osteogenesis. This protects against vessel stiffening in atherosclerosis and aging, and it is a vascular-homeostasis function of SIRT6. By preventing VSMCs from adopting an osteoblast-like phenotype, SIRT6 preserves arterial compliance and reduces the calcific burden of aged vessels. The mechanism complements SIRT6's inhibition of NF-κB and inflammatory gene programs in the vasculature.

SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and subsequently increases expression of glucose-dependent transporter 2 (GLUT2) in pancreatic β-cells. Directionally, SIRT6 activates FoxO1, which induces GLUT2. Higher GLUT2 restores glucose sensing and appropriate insulin release, maintaining systemic glucose tolerance. This complements SIRT6's role in β-cell metabolic health and its repression of TXNIP to preserve insulin secretion. By supporting β-cell identity and function, SIRT6 protects against the β-cell failure that characterizes type 2 diabetes, and its actions in β-cells illustrate how a nuclear sirtuin controls nutrient sensing.

SIRT6 inhibits transcription of Nkx3.2, a repressor of GATA5, thereby indirectly inducing GATA5 expression to prevent endothelial injury. Directionally, SIRT6 represses Nkx3.2, which derepresses GATA5. This balances vascular protective gene programs and illustrates a double-negative regulatory cascade through which SIRT6 controls endothelial gene expression. By removing the H3K9ac mark at the Nkx3.2 promoter, SIRT6 silences the repressor and allows GATA5 to be expressed. This chromatin-based mechanism is a clear example of SIRT6 acting as a master regulator of endothelial homeostasis through transcriptional cascades.

SIRT6 induces expression of GATA-binding protein 5 (GATA5) by deacetylating H3K9 at the Nkx3.2 promoter, preventing endothelial injury. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of GATA5 induction. GATA5 supports endothelial integrity and opposes dysfunction, and its induction by SIRT6 protects the vasculature from injury. This is a vascular-protective transcriptional output of SIRT6, achieved through repression of the Nkx3.2 repressor. The SIRT6-Nkx3.2-GATA5 axis exemplifies how SIRT6 controls downstream genes through cascades of transcription factors, and it connects epigenetic regulation to endothelial function and vascular disease.

SIRT6 deacetylates H3K9 at ERK1/2 gene promoters, inhibiting ERK1/2 expression and thereby dampening pro-hypertrophic MAPK signaling. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of ERK1/2 suppression. Reduced ERK signaling limits growth and fibrotic responses in the heart and vasculature, and it adds a MAPK-regulatory dimension to SIRT6's cardiovascular protection. By directly controlling the expression of the ERK1/2 genes themselves, rather than only their activity, SIRT6 provides sustained restraint of this pro-growth pathway, complementing its inhibition of IGF-Akt signaling in cardiac hypertrophy.

In pancreatic β-cells, SIRT6 deacetylates FoxO1 and increases GLUT2 expression to maintain glucose-sensing ability and systemic glucose tolerance. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically activates FoxO1 in β-cells. This preserves insulin-secretory competence under metabolic challenge, since GLUT2 is required for β-cells to sense glucose and respond appropriately. It mirrors SIRT6's broader metabolic-protective phenotype, including its repression of TXNIP to maintain glucose-stimulated insulin secretion. SIRT6's β-cell function is essential for preventing the glucose-intolerant state that characterizes type 2 diabetes.

SIRT6 promotes AMPK expression, which upregulates antioxidant genes MnSOD and catalase to suppress oxidative stress. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of AMPK induction. This couples SIRT6's chromatin functions to metabolic stress sensing, broadening SIRT6's protective network beyond deacetylation. Because AMPK also raises NAD+ and activates PGC-1α, SIRT6-dependent AMPK induction engages the full energy-sensing cascade. The antioxidant output of this axis protects cells from the oxidative damage that accumulates with age, and it complements SIRT6's direct roles in DNA repair and genome stability.

SIRT6 prevents TGF-β1-induced lung myofibroblast differentiation by inactivating TGF-β1/Smad3 signaling, limiting fibrogenesis. Directionally, SIRT6 sits upstream of TGF-β1/Smad3 blockade. This complements SIRT6's other antifibrotic actions in heart and kidney, and it positions SIRT6 as a broad suppressor of Smad3-driven fibrosis. By blocking myofibroblast differentiation, SIRT6 prevents the accumulation of contractile, matrix-producing cells that drive tissue scarring. SIRT6 activation therefore represents a potential strategy for pulmonary fibrosis and other fibrotic diseases where TGF-β signaling is central.

Despite higher SIRT6 protein, centenarian hMSCs show increased histone acetylation at H3K9, H3K18, and H3K27, confirming reduced deacetylase activity. Directionally, the variant sits upstream of weaker deacetylation. This indicates that the longevity benefit may hinge more on the ADP-ribosyltransferase than on the deacetylase function of SIRT6, and it reframes how active SIRT6 should be interpreted. The dissociation between increased protein abundance and reduced deacetylation highlights that SIRT6's two enzymatic activities are independently regulated. These findings are central to understanding the molecular basis of SIRT6's longevity association.

At late passages, centenarian-variant hMSCs show more Ki67-positive proliferating cells and fewer SA-β-gal-positive senescent cells, demonstrating delayed replicative senescence. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of senescence delay. This is a cellular correlate of exceptional human longevity, and it supports SIRT6 as a senescence-modulating factor. By delaying the entry into replicative senescence, the variant maintains the proliferative capacity and regenerative potential of stem cells. These observations connect the centenarian SIRT6 genotype to measurable cellular phenotypes associated with longevity.

Centenarian SIRT6 variants ameliorate multiple aging phenotypes in progerin-expressing hMSCs, including higher Ki67, reduced SA-β-gal, decreased p16/p21, reduced IL-6, and increased Lamin B1. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of progerin-stress resistance. This shows the variant buffers premature-aging pathology and ties SIRT6 to laminopathy resilience. By maintaining proliferation, reducing senescence markers, and lowering inflammatory output in progerin-stressed cells, the variants counteract key features of Hutchinson-Gilford progeria. These findings support SIRT6-boosting strategies for laminopathy and related premature-aging conditions.

Under progerin-induced stress, centenarian-variant hMSCs better maintain LINE-1 repression, with reduced ORF1p and ORF2p proteins. Directionally, CentSIRT6 sits upstream of continued LINE-1 silencing. This protects genome integrity against retrotransposition, and it connects the ADP-ribosyltransferase gain to repetitive-element control. By preserving heterochromatic silencing of LINE-1 elements during progerin stress, the variant maintains a key genome-defense mechanism. These results link the enhanced ADP-ribosylation activity of centenarian SIRT6 to the suppression of retroelement expression that destabilizes aging genomes.

SIRT6 mono-ADP-ribosylates KAP1 (a transcriptional corepressor), a modification that licenses recruitment of heterochromatin protein HP1α to repetitive DNA. Directionally, SIRT6 enzymatically ADP-ribosylates KAP1. This is distinct from its deacetylase action and is selectively enhanced by fucoidan and centenarian variants, and it is a key chromatin-silencing mechanism. By ADP-ribosylating KAP1, SIRT6 initiates the deposition of HP1α that packages LINE-1 retrotransposons into heterochromatin. This pathway is central to SIRT6's suppression of repetitive elements and genome stability.

Two independent SIRT6 transgenic strains show whole-body overexpression extending median lifespan of male mice by 14.5% and 9.9%, with no significant effect in females, associated with protection against lung tumors and preserved glucose tolerance. The effect is male-specific and tied to reduced serum IGF-1 and insulin/IGF-like growth-factor signaling. Directionally, SIRT6 overexpression sits upstream of male lifespan extension. The consistency across two independent strains strengthens the conclusion that SIRT6 promotes mammalian longevity, and the male specificity highlights the interplay between sirtuins and sex hormones in lifespan regulation.

Male SIRT6 transgenics have lower serum IGF-1 and reduced downstream insulin/IGF-1-like signaling (AKT, pAKT); reduced insulin/IGF-1-like signaling is strongly associated with increased longevity in model organisms, providing the leading explanation for SIRT6's male-specific lifespan extension. Directionally, SIRT6-mediated inhibition of IGF-1 signaling sits upstream of lifespan extension. By suppressing the growth-promoting IGF-AKT axis, SIRT6 may recapitulate the longevity benefits of reduced insulin/IGF signaling. This mechanism connects SIRT6 to one of the most conserved longevity pathways across species.
